Don’t Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025: Do you share your
opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay
silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I
often found myself in the second group. A little
black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I
considered speaking up. (A)조롱을 당하거나 틀리거
나 한 결과들이 늘 나의 마음에 걸렸습니다.
Then, after a particularly heated conversation in
class, I asked myself, “What am I afraid of?” I was
scared that bad things would happen, but I never
thought about good things. When I noticed others
taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same
in order to ⓐ[withdraw / participate]. Many people
are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it
anyway because they think it’s worth it. So I left
my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew
intellectually and socially by expressing myself more
ⓑ[clearly / incoherently]. I got closer to friends who
liked how open I was with them. Now I have more
people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and
learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of
expressing yourself can be extremely ⓒ[unfulfilling /
rewarding] in unexpected ways.

Welcome to a new season of High School
Magazine. To start off the new school year on the
right foot, we asked some of our recent
ⓐgraduates to give us tips on how to succeed in
the coming year and beyond.
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more ⓑtalented
than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt
small in comparison. I thought about giving up my
dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I
happened to see a drawing I had won an award
for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was
embarrassed because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make sense to compare yourself to Internet
ⓒpersonalities or even people in your real life.
Maybe they had an advantage, or even a
disadvantage, that you didn’t. If you are going to
compare yourself to anyone, the only ⓓfair
comparison is “yesterday-you.” Only you know
where you started and how much effort you’ve put
in. I couldn’t see the progress in my ability when I
only compared myself to others. Everyone develops
differently. I’m able to see now the drawing in the
kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make.
It is ⓔempowering to see how I have improved
rather than to envy the success of others. Your
competition isn’t the person next door or the
influencer on social media: it’s you.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: a person who has completed a course ofstudy, especially from a school or university
ⓑ: having a natural ability or skill in a particulararea, such as art, music, or sports
ⓒ: the characteristic set of behaviors, attitudes,and emotions that make a person unique
ⓓ: treating all people or things equally andjustly, without favoritism or bias
ⓔ: giving someone the authority or power to dosomething; making someone feel stronger ormore confident
solution: ⓒ의 personalities는 문맥상 인물들이라는 의미로  ‘a person, especially one who is notable or has a distinctive character (특히 유명하거나 독특한 성격을 가진 사람)’으로 풀이되지만, the characteristic set of behaviors, attitudes, and emotions that make a person unique는 ‘사람을 독특하게 만드는 행동, 태도, 감정의 특성 모음’이라는 뜻을 가진 ‘개성’의 영영풀이이다.

One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is that it
would let people disagree with or be unhappy with
a post without having to say something bad about
ⓐit. This could help make conversations on social
media platforms more (A)[open / confidential], honest,
and respectful. A “Dislike” button could also help
figure out what users like or find useful. By letting
people express what ⓑthey don’t like about a post,
content creators can get useful feedback and learn
what ⓒtheir audience likes and doesn’t like.
Jimin
The “Dislike” button can definitely be a useful tool
to measure online engagement, but there are more
negative effects than the positive. The presence of
“Dislike” buttons and other negative replies
illustrates how (B)[unfriendly / friendly] social media
can be. Many businesses directly ask for “5-star”
ratings because anything less may actually hurt
ⓓtheir reputation. A “Dislike” button encourages
users to take advantage of the system rather than
provide an honest opinion. While it may be useful
for creators, it can also be (C)[harmful / harmless]
to both ⓔthem and everyone else.

Lucia
Many gifts are thoughtful and ⓐpersonalized for
the receiver. However, with online shopping apps
and convenience stores everywhere, many gifts are
also given just so that the giver isn’t caught
empty-handed. I don’t see a problem with regifting
common gifts until they find a home with someone
who will ⓑappreciate them. The giving of the gift
is the thoughtful gesture, not the actual gift itself.
For this reason, (A)여러분은 버려질 수도 있는, 선물
받은 뭔가를 남에게 선물로 주는 것에 대해 죄책감을
느껴서는 안 된다.

I don’t think regifting is a good thing. A gift is
something you receive from someone who put
thought and effort into it. A gift is more than just

receiver. Something like that shouldn’t just be given
away to another person. Also, if the original giver
finds out that their gift was given away, it could cause
ⓓhard feelings. All in all, I don’t think regifting is
worth the ⓔtrouble that it could cause. Just keep
the gift as a reminder of a good relationship.

body:
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more (A)[difficulties / advantages] balancing
school and personal life. I would get excited,
anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then
separately. I would get exhausted when I had to
write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster
between friends, and respond to the comments on
my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of
responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that
was when I read an article with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. Believing that
everything was in my circle of influence left me
stressed out and constantly exhausted. By
(B)[preserving / wasting] less energy on my circle of
concern, I was able to invest more energy into
things that mattered. I no longer worry about what
my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I
don’t get anxious over what might be on the test,
and instead I put in every effort to understand the
concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental
and physical energy into my circle of (C)influence /
concern] eating healthy, staying in shape, and
working hard.

Charlie
One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is
(A)[what / that] it would let people disagree with or
be unhappy with a post without having to say
something bad about it. This could help make
conversations on social media platforms more open,
honest, and (B)[respectfully / respectful]. A “Dislike”

(B)

solution: (A) 주어 One possible benefit의 주격보어로 뒤 문장이 완전 한 절 (it would ~ about it)을 이루고 있으므로 명사절을 이 끄는 접속사 that이 알맞다. (B) 동사 make가 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하게 만들 다)’의 5형식 구문으로 사용될 때, 목적격보어로 형용사가 오므 로, ‘help+동사원형(~하는 것을 돕다)’ 구문의 동사원형 make 의 목적격보어로 쓰인 형용사 more open, honest와 등위 접 속사 and로 연결되는 형용사 respectful이 알맞다. (C) 사역동사 let은 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하게 하다)' 의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동의 관 계일 경우 목적격보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)을 쓴다. 따라서 letting의 목적어 people이 ’표현하는‘ 주체로 능동 관계이므로 목적격보어로 동사원형 express가 알맞다. 비상(홍민표) 1과

Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I

life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get

courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I

The article advised me (A)[to draw / draw] two big
circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle
is my circle of influence, and I have direct control
over the things ⓑinside it: what I eat and drink,
how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger
circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry
about but have no direct control over. For example,
I have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research (B)[that / what] I do for it.
ⓒBelieving that everything was in my circle of
influence left me stressed out and constantly
(C)[exhausted / exhausting]. By wasting ⓓmore
energy on my circle of concern, I was able to
invest more energy into things that mattered. I no
longer worry about what my friends think, and I
focus on my own actions. I don’t get anxious over

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) ‘~에게 …을 조언하다’라는 뜻의 ‘advise+목적어+목적격보 어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문이므로, 과거형 advised의 목적격보 어인 to부정사 to draw가 알맞다. (B) 동사 do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(I do for it)을 이끌 어, 선행사 the amount of research를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. (C) 동사 leave는 ‘leave+목적어+목적격보어(‘~을 …상태로 남 기다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 목적격보어로 형용사 또는 분 사가 올 수 있다. 동사 left의 목적어인 me가 ‘스트레스를 받고 지치게 된’ 대상이므로 목적격보어 stressed out과 등위접속사 and로 연결되는 과거분사형 형용사 exhausted가 알맞다.

talk,
share
my ideas, and learn new things.

can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Nahyeon Kim 2024 Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more talented than
me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in
comparison. I thought about giving up my dream
of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to
see a drawing (A)[that / what] I had won an award
for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was
embarrassed because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make sense (B)[to compare / to be compared]
yourself to Internet personalities or even people in
your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or
even a disadvantage, that you didn’t. If you are
going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair
comparison is “yesterday-you.” ⓐ여러분만이 여러분
이 어디에서 시작했고 얼마나 큰 노력을 했는지 알고
있습니다. I couldn’t see the progress in my ability
when I only compared myself to others. Everyone
develops differently. I’m able to see now the
drawing in the kitchen (C)[were / was] full of

Charlie
One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is that it
would let people disagree with or be unhappy with
a post without having to say something bad about
it. This could help make conversations on social
media platforms more open, honest, and respectful.
A “Dislike” button could also help figure out what
users like or find useful. By letting people express
what they don’t like about a post, content creators
can get useful feedback and learn what their
audience likes and doesn’t like.
Jimin
The “Dislike” button can definitely be a useful tool
to measure online engagement, but there are more
negative effects than the positive. The presence of
“Dislike” buttons and other negative replies
illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many
businesses directly ask for “5-star” ratings because
anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A
“Dislike” button encourages users to take advantage
of the system rather than provide an honest
opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can
also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

ways in which social media can foster morepositive interactions
pros and cons of the existence of the 'dislike'button on social media platforms
the impact of the 'dislike' button online on thegrowth of creators and businesses
various reasons why the 'dislike' button on socialmedia increases user engagement

body:
Charlie
One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is that it
would let people disagree with or be unhappy with
a post without having to say something bad about
it. This could help make conversations on social
media platforms more open, honest, and respectful.
A “Dislike” button could also help figure out what
users like or find useful. By letting people express
what they don’t like about a post, content creators
can get useful feedback and learn what their
audience likes and doesn’t like.
Jimin
The “Dislike” button can definitely be a useful tool
to measure online engagement, but there are more
negative effects than the positive. The presence of
“Dislike” buttons and other negative replies
illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many
businesses directly ask for “5-star” ratings because
anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A
“Dislike” button encourages users to take advantage
of the system rather than provide an honest
opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can
also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Charlie believes that the "Dislike" button couldcontribute to more open, honest and respectfulconversation on social media.
Jimin asserts that the "Dislike" button may havea detrimental impact on the reputation of contentcreators and businesses.
Charlie contends that the "Dislike" button can assistcontent creators in gaining a clearer understandingof their audience's preferences.
Jimin argues that the "Dislike" button encouragesusers to exploit the system rather than providehonest feedback.
In contrast to Charlie, Jimin thinks that the "Dislike"button is not an effective tool for gauging userengagement.

Welcome to a new season of High School
Magazine. To start off the new school year on the
right foot, we asked some of our recent
ⓐgraduates to give us tips on how to succeed in
the coming year and beyond.
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more ⓑtalented
than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt
small in comparison. I thought about giving up my
dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I
happened to see a drawing I had won an award
for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was
embarrassed because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make sense to compare yourself to Internet
ⓒpersonalities or even people in your real life.
Maybe they had an advantage, or even a
disadvantage, that you didn’t. If you are going to
compare yourself to anyone, the only ⓓfair
comparison is “yesterday-you.” Only you know
where you started and how much effort you’ve put
in. I couldn’t see the progress in my ability when I
only compared myself to others. Everyone develops
differently. I’m able to see now the drawing in the
kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make.
It is ⓔempowering to see how I have improved
rather than to envy the success of others. Your
competition isn’t the person next door or the
influencer on social media: it’s you.

윗글을 읽고 알 수 있는 내용으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: the reason Nahyeon wanted to become an illustrator in high school
the reason Nahyeon considered giving up her dream of becoming an artist in university
the feeling Nahyeon had when she happened to see the drawing she won an award for from middle school
the benefits Nahyeon gained from comparing herself to others
the fair comparison Nahyeon believes in

body:
Elias Walter Class of 2025: Do you share your
opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay
silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I
often found myself in the second group. A little
black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I
considered speaking up. The consequences of being
ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.
Then, after a particularly heated conversation in
class, I asked myself, “What am I afraid of?” I was
scared that bad things would happen, but I never
thought about good things. When I noticed others
taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same
in order to participate. Many people are scared to
speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because
they think it’s worth it. So I left my comfort zone
and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and
socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got
closer to friends who liked how open I was with
them. Now I have more people with whom I can
talk,
share
my ideas, and learn new things.
Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself
can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

윗글의 내용을 가장 잘 이해한 사람들로 짝지어진 것은?

∎ Mr. A: Elias hesitated to speak up in class
discussions, gripped by a profound fear
of mockery and the possibility of error.
∎ Ms. B: Elias was initially not interested in sharing
his opinion in class discussions but
changed his mind after he realized the
benefits of expressing himself.
∎ Mr. C: Elias preferred to stay reserved during
class discussions, and after observing
others venturing out, he decided to
stay in his comfort zone.
∎ Ms. D: Elias discovered that by voicing his
thoughts, he experienced growth not
only in his intellectual capacity but
also in his social connections.
∎ Mr. E: Elias reflects on his decision to speak
up and feels that the risks he took did
not yield the expected benefits.

(→ 수업 토론에서 목소리를 내야겠 다고 생각할 때마다 자신의 안에 있는 작은 블랙홀이 목소리 를 억눌렀다고 했으므로, 자신의 의견을 내는 데 관심이 없었 던 것은 아님을 알 수 있다.) ∎ Mr. C: Elias는 수업 토론 중에 침묵을 지키기를 선호했고, 다른 사람들이 위험을 감수하는 모습을 본 후 결국 그는 그의 안전지대에 남기로 결정을 내렸다. (→ 안전지대를 벗어나 목 소리를 내기 시작했다.) ∎ Mr. E: Elias는 목소리를 내는 결정을 되돌아보며, 자신이 감 수한 위험들이 기대한 혜택을 가져오지 않았다고 느꼈다. (→ 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것이 예상치 못한 방식으로 매우 보람이 있을 수 있음을 깨달았다.)

body:
Charlie
One possible benefit of a “Dislike” button is that it
would let people disagree with or be unhappy with
a post without having to say something bad about
it. This could help make conversations on social
media platforms more open, honest, and respectful.
A “Dislike” button could also help figure out what
users like or find useful. By letting people express
what they don’t like about a post, content creators
can get useful feedback and learn what their
audience likes and doesn’t like.
Jimin
The “Dislike” button can definitely be a useful tool
to measure online engagement, but there are more
negative effects than the positive. The presence of
“Dislike” buttons and other negative replies
illustrates how unfriendly social media can be. Many
businesses directly ask for “5-star” ratings because
anything less may actually hurt their reputation. A
“Dislike” button encourages users to take advantage
of the system rather than provide an honest
opinion. While it may be useful for creators, it can
also be harmful to both them and everyone else.

body:
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022: As I worked
through my second year into my third in college, I
had more troubles balancing school and personal
life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and
bored all at once and then separately. I would get
exhausted when I had to write a report for my
courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and
respond to the comments on my online journal. I
was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns,
and anxieties, and that was when I read an article
with a simple insight.
The article advised me to draw two big circles,
with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my
circle of influence, and I have direct control over
the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I
behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle
is called my circle of concern: things I worry about
but have no direct control over. For example, I
have no direct control over how my professor will
react to my report, but I do have control over the
amount of research I do for it. Believing that
everything was in my circle of influence left me
stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting
less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to
invest more energy into things that mattered. I no
longer worry about what my friends think, and I
focus on my own actions. I don’t get anxious over
what might be on the test, and instead I put in
every effort to understand the concepts themselves.
Now, __________________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: I find myself trying to change situations that areinherently beyond my control
I am confident that my actions and thoughtscan make a significant difference in the world
I focus my energy on things I can control, likeeating healthy, staying in shape, and workinghard
I believe that larger transformations have a moreprofound impact on my life
I concentrate on pursuing concrete and achievablegoals rather than abstract ones
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024: In high school,
everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I
dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university,
though, everyone seemed much more talented than
me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in
comparison. I thought about giving up my dream
of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to
see a drawing I had won an award for from middle
school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed
because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to
oranges, and they’re right. That’s why it doesn’t
make sense to compare yourself to Internet
personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe
they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage,
that you didn’t. If you are going to compare
yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is
“yesterday-you.” Only you know where you started
and how much effort you’ve put in. I couldn’t see
the progress in my ability when I only compared
myself to others. Everyone _______________________. I’m
able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full
of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering
to see how I have improved rather than to envy
the success of others. Your competition isn’t the
person next door or the influencer on social media:
it’s you.
choices: faces the same challenges as you
is perfect and never makes mistakes

body:
When you think of curry, do you think of your
favorite spicy dish from a local Indian restaurant or
ⓐmilder something spread over steamed white rice?
There are different types of curries all around the
world. Curry comes in many flavors, and the recipes
are different ⓑdepending on where you are in the
world. For example, Japanese curry differs significantly
from Indian curry despite ⓒsharing the same origin.
The term “curry” comes from the Tamil word “kari,”
ⓓwhich means “sauce.” According to The Japan
Times, curry made its way to Japan from India in
the 1850s and 1860s, ⓔwhen the country began
trading with British sailors. The Royal Navy
introduced curry to Japan in the late 19th century,
and the Japanese Navy adapted it to suit their own
tastes and needs. Not surprisingly, the Japanese
curry (or kare raisu) ⓕlooks quite differently from
the Indian version.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?

Some people love this combination, while others
can’t seem to stand it. It can even cause quite
heated arguments. If you haven’t guessed already,
it’s the tasty or nasty — depending on your taste —
ham and pineapple pizza. The man who created
this pizza was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek
immigrant from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not
want to stick to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like
pepperoni and mushrooms. He spread canned
pineapple and sliced ham onto a pizza and called it
“the Hawaiian” because that’s what was written on
the pineapple can. Little did he know that he had
created a classic combination. Even now, ____________
______________________________________. In Italy, however,
most people find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
Why is Hawaiian pizza so divisive? The
combination is not that odd. Pineapple and ham is
not the only fruit and meat pairing in kitchens
around the world.

the challenges of creating new pizza toppings worldwide
the historical origin of pizza and its many variations

A very popular dessert in Thailand is sweet, sticky
rice topped with fresh mango and coconut milk.
(A)망고 찰밥은 사랑하지 않기 매우 어려운 요리다.
Rice is one of the world’s most consumed grains,
so it should not be surprising that it can be
combined with other interesting ingredients. One of
those ingredients is fruit, which is nutritious, sweet,
and plentiful in many parts of the world. The
combination of fruit and rice may seem unusual,
but it’s actually quite common.
According to the Tourism Authority of Thailand,
neither mango nor sticky rice is native to Thailand.
Mangoes are native to Myanmar and India, and
sticky rice is commonly eaten in Laos, which shares
a border with Thailand. This suggests that the roots
of the dish are probably a result of the mixing of
cultures in Southeast Asia. Rice is usually thought of
as a food that is eaten as a meal, but its use as a
dessert shows how simple ingredients can create
innovative, wonderful treats.

The main difference between Japanese curry and
Indian curry is the spice mix that is used. In Japan,
curry spices come in the form of small, pre-packaged
blocks, which are sold in grocery stores. On the
other hand, Indian cooks do not typically use
pre-mixed spices. They create their own mixtures of
turmeric, ginger, and other spices to make curry.
Since pre-packaged spices are not commonly used,
Indian curries vary in color and texture: some are
bright yellow, while others are deep red. Some are
thin and soupy, while others are thick and dense.
The curry that we eat in Korea today was
introduced by the Japanese. It became popular in
the late 1960s when (A)기성품 카레 가루가 빠르고
간단한 식사를 준비하는 것을 쉽게 만들었다. Therefore,
the curry served in Korea is similar to Japanese
curry, with the main difference being that Korean
curry is bright yellow because it contains turmeric, a
deep yellow spice.

Some people love this combination, while others
can’t seem to stand it. It can even cause quite
heated arguments. If you haven’t guessed already,
it’s the tasty or nasty — depending on your taste —
ham and pineapple pizza. The man who created
this pizza was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek
immigrant from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not
want to stick to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like
pepperoni and mushrooms. He spread canned
pineapple and sliced ham onto a pizza and called it
“the Hawaiian” (A)________________ that’s what was
written on the pineapple can. ⓐ그가 고전적인 조합
을 만들어냈다는 것을 그는 거의 알지 못했다. Even
now, in the U.S. and U.K., no pizza menu seems
complete without it. In Italy, however, most people
find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
Why is Hawaiian pizza so divisive? The
combination is not that odd. Pineapple and ham is
not the only fruit and meat pairing in kitchens
around the world. In France, duck is paired with a
sweet orange sauce, and American Thanksgiving
turkey dinner would not be complete without
cranberry sauce. Many people enjoy salty and sweet
flavor combinations, (B)________________ some others
prefer to keep those tastes as far from each other
as possible.

(B)

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area’s
biggest predators, came with little warning in the
sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge
of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark ⓐ[tracking
/ to track] her. In an instant, she swam into a crack
to escape, but the shark was faster.
(A) The next day, I was relieved to see that she
had survived. She was weak, and her colors
were not as bright. I checked on her every day,
wondering if that day would be the last. It was
emotionally painful ⓑ[to witness / witness]
these things happening to her.
(B) The shark ⓒ[had taken / has taken] a bite of
one of her arms and was waiting for her. I
wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She
managed to get deeper into the crack, but she
was bleeding.
(C) After a while, the shark lost interest, and the
octopus used the opportunity to get back to
her den, without one of her arms. She was in
serious danger because her arms function like
the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
solution: ⓐ 지각동사 see는 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 의 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 원형부정사 또는 현재분사를 쓴 다. 동사 saw의 목적어 a shark가 ‘추적을 하는’ 주체로 능동 관계이므로 목적격보어로 현재분사 tracking이 알맞다. ⓑ 가주어 It에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로, to부정사 to witness가 알맞다. ⓒ 상어가 ‘그녀의 팔 중 하나를 물어뜯은’ 것이 ‘그녀를 기다 리고 있는’ 것보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거진행형 동사 was waiting보다 앞선 시점을 나타내는 과거완료 had taken이 알맞다.

body:
I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South
Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over
20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold
sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among
the dense seaweed forests (A)[which / where] I met
an octopus.
I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of
shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap
and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of
the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it
disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of
seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring
at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary
creature! I wondered what would happen if I
(B)[kept / had kept] watching it. To see the world
from the octopus’s perspective, I left a camera near
the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped
the environment around the den. (C)[Expected /
Expecting] some drama to come, I waited.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 장소를 나타내는 선행사 the dense seaweed forests를 수 식하는 완전한 절(I met an octopus)을 이끌고 있으므로 관계 부사 where가 알맞다. (B) ‘계속 관찰하면 어떤 일이 일어날지 궁금하다‘는 의미로 미 래의 일을 나타내므로 가정법이 아니라 조건문이다. 따라서 주 절의 과거동사 wondered에 세제를 일치시켜 종속절에도 조동 사 will의 과거형인 would가 쓰였으므로, if절에도 동사 keep의 과거형 kept를 쓰는 것이 알맞다. (C) 분사구문으로, 주절의 주어인 ‘I’가 ‘기대하는’ 주체이며 목 적어로 some drama가 오므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Expecting이 알맞다.

often. After about a month, it came near me. I put
my hand out, and it reached out to me.
(A) I started reading books about octopuses, but I
wanted to learn more about this marvelous
creature. The first thing I learned was that “it”
was a “she.”
(B) To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way

toward the surface.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?

A short while later, I saw that the wound had
healed. ⓐTo my amazement, a little arm started to
grow back, and she started to become active again.
I started to compare my life to life in the
unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in
life. I began to spend more time with my family
and friends, and I even started to dive with my
young son. He became just as interested in her as I
was. As the octopus’s arm became more functional,
I felt things in my life were improving too.
An octopus’s average life is about a year, ⓑwhich
ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after
meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It
was bittersweet knowing her
final
days were
approaching even though she would bear young.
ⓒAfter mating, she didn’t come out of her den.
There would be no feeding or hunting. She was
timing her final moments for the hatching of her
eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few
months later, my son found a little octopus. We
believe her story continues on.
I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing
wildness she represented. I built a relationship with
her and witnessed her life up to the final moments.
I saw her from a perspective that I could not have
had ⓓwithout this experience. She was smart,
sensitive, and strong, often ⓔgoing through rough
and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she
committed herself to protecting the birth of her
young before she died. As a human being, I found
something noble in that sacrifice. She was not
simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just
as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all
have our own stories to tell.
choices: ⓐ To my amazement, a little arm started togrow back= I was amazed that a little arm started togrow back.
ⓑ which ends after reproducing= and it ends after reproducing
ⓓ without this experience= if it were not for this experience
ⓔ going through rough and tough days justlike humans do= and she went through rough and toughdays just like humans do
solution: 주절의 동사 saw로 보아 과거의 상황에 대한 가정으로 ‘without 가정법 과거완료’ 구문으로, 주절에는 ‘조동사의 과거 형+have+p.p.’를 쓰고, 조건절에는 ‘if+S+had p.p.‘를 쓴다. 따 라서 ⓓ without this experience는 ’if it had not been for this experience’로 고쳐야 한다.

we all have our own stories to tell

now and then?

that hermit crabs are really social.

Sometimes they even trade shells with each
other.

choices: What I’m saying is that they live in groups andhelp each other
What I mean is that they stay together andassist each other
My point is that they stick together and lendeach other a hand
What I want to say is that they form groupsand support one another
What I’m trying to avoid saying is that theycooperate and live as a group
solution: 소라게의 사회적인 특성이 개미나 벌처럼 비슷하냐고 묻는 질 문의 답이자, 뒤에 이어지는 내용에서 그들은 서로 껍질을 교 환하기도 한다고 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 상대방이 완전 히 이해하지 못했을 수도 있을 때 다시 설명하거나 자신의 요 점을 강조하는 역할을 하는 ‘What I’m saying is that ~‘ 또는 ’What I want to say is that ~‘ 또는 ’What I mean is that ~ ‘의 표현을 사용하여 ’내가 말하는 건, 소라게가 무리를 지어 살면서 서로 돕는다는 거야‘와 같은 표현이 들어간다. 따라서 ❺ ’내가 말하지 않으려고 하는 것은 그들이 협력하며 무리 지 어 산다는 것이야‘는 알맞지 않다.

body:
I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South
Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over
20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold
sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among
the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.
I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of
shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap
and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the (A)_____________
of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it
disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of
seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring
at me out of a little gap. What a(n) (B)______________
creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept
watching it. To see the world from the octopus’s
perspective, I left a camera near the den and
started visiting regularly. I even mapped the
environment around the den. Expecting some drama
to come, I waited.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
solution: (A) 문어는 조개더미 속에 숨어 있다가, 갑자기 튀어나와 믈고 기를 잡았다는 흐름으로 ‘영리함, 기발함’을 뜻하는 ingenuity 또는 cleverness가 알맞다. (B) 문어는 해초를 사용해서 자신을 가린 뒤 틈으로 나를 관찰 하였고, 그 생물체를 지켜보다 보면 무언가 흥미로운 일이 일 어날 것만 같았다는 흐름이므로 ‘특별한’의 뜻을 가진 extraordinary 또는 exceptional이 알맞다.

body:
An octopus’s average life is about a year, which
ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after
meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It
was bittersweet knowing her
final
days were
approaching even though she would bear young.
After mating, she didn’t come out of her den.
There would be no feeding or hunting. She was
timing her final moments for the hatching of her
eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few
months later, my son found a little octopus. We
believe her story continues on.
I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing
wildness she represented. I built a relationship with
her and witnessed her life up to the final moments.
(A)나는 이 경험이 없었다면 가질 수 없었을 관점으로
그녀를 보았다. She was smart, sensitive, and strong,
often going through rough and tough days just like
humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to
protecting the birth of her young before she died.
As a human being, (B)________________________________.
She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of
this world just as I am a part of it now, and in
that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: I felt helpless in the face of her fate.
I believed her sacrifice was unnecessary
I found something noble in that sacrifice
I found her behavior strange and confusing
I felt resentment toward her natural life cycle
solution: 문어는 영리하고 예민하며 강했고, 사람처럼 거칠고 힘든 날들 을 자주 겪어냈고, 결국 그녀는 죽기 전에 새끼의 탄생을 지키 기 위해 자신을 헌신했으며, 필자는 문어가 단순한 동물이 아 니라, 자신과 마찬가지로 이 세상의 중요한 일부로서, 그녀의 삶과 희생에 의미가 있다고 말하는 흐름으로 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘나 는 그 희생에서 고귀한 어떤 것을 발견했다’가 가장 알맞다.

toward the surface.

peacefully ⓐ[lay / lying] on the floats near the pier
looked like melting chocolate. They didn’t smell
ⓑ[pleasant / pleasantly] up close, yet their cuteness
delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the
famous spot that appears in most movies and TV
shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise,
ⓒ[enjoyed / enjoying] the view of the city. As we
passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly,

Where: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia  When: July
The Naadam Festival celebrates Mongolia’s unique
culture, with events that were popular in the 13th
century. The festival features three sports
competitions: wrestling, archery, and horse racing.
In the wrestling competition, hundreds of male
players participate. In the archery competition,
ⓐeach athlete is given four arrows to hit targets 65

30 kilometers. ⓑThe participants in the horse race

November

“Day of the Dead.” ⓒIt is one of the most
important holidays in Mexico, where people believe
that the souls of the dead can return to the living
world for a reunion with their loved ones as the
gates of heaven are opened during this holiday.

(A)______________________________________________________.
In their homes, ⓓthey build stands which they put
photos of the dead along with their favorite foods
and other meaningful objects.

Hogmanay is a Scottish way of celebrating the
new year. The origin of Hogmanay is unclear, but
some people believe it comes from Northern
Europe.
Hogmanay features a fire-lit parade and singing of
traditional songs at night. The most popular custom
is the practice of “first footing.” At night,
ⓔneighbors visit one another and share traditional
food gifts such as black fruit cake and drink.
Interestingly, ⓕbeing visited by a male visitor with
dark hair considers good luck.

Naadam Festival
Where: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia  When: July
The Naadam Festival celebrates Mongolia’s unique
culture, with events that were popular in the 13th
century. The festival features three sports
competitions: wrestling, archery, and horse racing.
In the wrestling competition, hundreds of male
players participate. In the archery competition,
ⓐeach athlete is given four arrows to hit targets 65
to 75 meters away. A horse race can be as long as
30 kilometers. ⓑThe participants in the horse race
is children 5 to 13 years old.
Día de los Muertos
Where: Mexico  When: end of October to early
November
Día de los Muertos is commonly known as the
“Day of the Dead.” ⓒIt is one of the most
important holidays in Mexico, where people believe
that the souls of the dead can return to the living
world for a reunion with their loved ones as the
gates of heaven are opened during this holiday.
To celebrate Día de los Muertos, Mexicans gather
(A)______________________________________________________.
In their homes, ⓓthey build stands which they put
photos of the dead along with their favorite foods
and other meaningful objects.
Hogmanay
Where: Scotland  When: December 31 to January 1
Hogmanay is a Scottish way of celebrating the
new year. The origin of Hogmanay is unclear, but
some people believe it comes from Northern
Europe.
Hogmanay features a fire-lit parade and singing of
traditional songs at night. The most popular custom
is the practice of “first footing.” At night,
ⓔneighbors visit one another and share traditional
food gifts such as black fruit cake and drink.
Interestingly, ⓕbeing visited by a male visitor with
dark hair considers good luck.

to forget their sorrow and move on quickly totheir work
to drive away the souls of the dead to wherethey should be

dots will be a representation of who you are at this

can. Write one or two words to describe one
aspect of yourself next to each dot. (A)상들, 자격증

past and present achievements, interests, and strengths.
Parents, teachers, friends, and others ⓔyou trust
them can also provide insight into you that you
may not have noticed. If you think it describes you,
ⓕwrite down it as a new dot. Hopefully doing this
exercise will show you that there’s more to being
you than you may have thought.

body:
Fill in the Gaps
To reach your goal of becoming a musician, you
need to fill in the gaps between the dots to create
a path toward your goal. Do you need to work on
voice techniques or set up a personal website to
promote yourself first? You can plan other paths by
researching what essential skills, training or
education, or type of personality you may need to
achieve a particular goal. Talking to or shadowing
people (A)[considering / considered] to be
successful is a great way to learn about a specific
profession too. As you fill in each gap with a new
dot, you can decide what to do next. Each path is
unique and has different challenges.
Take the Next Steps
Now, instead of aimlessly trying random things,
you can look at your map to see what to do next.
Just look for a gap to fill. (B)[Decide / Deciding]
which gap to fill is up to you, but your dot map
should show you that whatever you choose, you
will be moving toward your goal. There is no need
to rush anything though. Take your time filling the
gaps. Since you’ve designed your own map, each
gap you fill and dot you make “levels you up.”
If you’ve made it this far, you probably realize
some dots will take time to complete, and other
dots will take great effort. No one knows what kind
of person (C)[you will / will you] be five or ten
years down the road, so each investment you make
in yourself now will grow into expertise and
experience in the future. ⓐ점들은 현재의 여러분 스
스로를 보고 그러고 나서 가능한 한 많은 미래들 속의
여러분 자신을 상상하는 방법입니다. It’s up to you
to start connecting your dots now.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 앞의 명사 people을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리 로, people이 ‘여겨지는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘consider A to be B(A를 B라고 여기다)’의 to부정사구 to be successful 이 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘A be considered to be B(A가 B 라고 여겨지다)’의 과거분사 considered가 적절하다. (B) 문장의 동사로 is가 있으므로 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구를 이루는 Deciding이 적절하다. 참고로, 뒤에 동명사의 목적어로 의문사구인 which gap to fill이 쓰였다. (C) ’what kind ~ road’는 동사 knows의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의 문문이므로, 의문사구인 what kind of person 뒤에 ‘주어+조동 사+동사원형~’의 평서문 어순을 이루는 you will이 적절하다.

body:
MYTH: Selecting what’s “hot” at the moment is
desirable.
FACT: No one can predict the future.
New career fields and jobs emerge every year as
society, technology, and economic trends change.
Therefore, it is not advised to select a major or
(A)[pursue / pursuing] a career just because it’s
popular now. ⓐ그러한 선택을 하는 것은 여러분 자신
의 관심사들, 헌신, 그리고 꿈을 존중하지 않는 것이다.
Those qualities are more important than any current
trend that may disappear soon.
MYTH: If X is happy in a particular field, I will be
happy, too.
FACT: You are not X.
Simply speaking, everyone is different. Even if X is
someone (B)[whom / with whom] you have a lot in
common, what works for that X may not necessarily
work for you. If someone you know has a career
that interests you, get more details about the
career in terms of the job description and the skills
(C)[required / requiring]. Choosing the best career
for you is more important than choosing one too
quickly.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 문장의 진주어로 쓰인 to select 이하의 to부정사구 내에서 to에 이어진 동사원형 select와 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결되 므로 동사원형 pursue가 적절하다. (B) 뒤에 완전한 절인 you have a lot in common이 이어지므 로 ’전치사+관계대명사‘인 with whom이 적절하다. 참고로, 목 적격 관계대명사 whom 뒤에는 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절이 와야 한다. (C) 흐름상 앞의 명사구 the skills를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 the skills가 ’요구되는‘ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 required가 적절하다.

“What do you want to do in the future?” Parents
and teachers ask students this question all the time.
But how many students actually know what they
want to do in the future? Many students are either
unsure of what they know or ⓐconfused about
how to find the right career. The following may
help students discover a new way to look at
themselves and ⓑdesign a path for their future.
Discover Yourself
It’s hard to climb a mountain without preparation,
and designing a career path requires preparation
too. Begin your career map by taking a blank piece
of paper and ⓒdrawing some dots on it. These
dots will be a representation of who you are at this
moment in time, so make ⓓas more dots as you
can. Write one or two words to describe one
aspect of yourself next to each dot. (A)상들, 자격증
들, 그리고 학교에서 수강된 교과목들은 시작할 훌륭
한 지점들입니다. You can also think about your
past and present achievements, interests, and strengths.
Parents, teachers, friends, and others ⓔyou trust
them can also provide insight into you that you
may not have noticed. If you think it describes you,
ⓕwrite down it as a new dot. Hopefully doing this
exercise will show you that there’s more to being
you than you may have thought.

body:
Examine Your Resources
Now, take a step back and look at your dots. A
good idea at this stage is to start categorizing your
dots. Do you see any patterns emerging? For
example, you might have several dots that highlight
scientific skills or maybe some dots that point to
creativity. These patterns may point to something
that is meaningful to you. Another perspective is to
look at what is missing from your map, (A)[what /
which] you can call “gaps.” For example, you may
feel that you need some work on mathematics or a
foreign language. At such a young age, you probably
don’t have certain skills: your technical knowledge
might be at a beginner level, or your physical
conditioning might need work. Noticing these gaps
will help you in the next steps of your map.
Set Up Goals
By comparing your strengths and weaknesses, or
the dots and the gaps, your map should show you
(B)[what / that] you possess and what you need to
work on. Now, think of a long-term goal, like
becoming a musician. Your goal doesn’t have to be
realistic; remember that the purpose of having the
goal clearly (C)[write / written] is to map out a way
to get there. ⓐ여러분이 어디로 가고 싶은지를 이해
하는 것은 중요한 단계이고, 따라서 그다음 단계는 그
목표로 나아가기 위해 계획을 짜는 것이다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) ‘call+목적어+목적격보어(~를 …라고 부르다)’의 5형식에서 call의 목적어 없이 목적격보어 “gaps”만 있는 불완전한 절 you can call “gaps”를 이끌어 선행사인 what is missing from your map을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 계속 적 용법의 목적격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 참고로, 관계 대명사 what은 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것(들)’을 뜻한다. (B) 4형식 구문인 ‘show+간접목적어+직접목적어(~에게 …을 보여 주다)’의 직접목적어 자리에서 ‘~한 것(들)’이라는 의미로 동사 (possess)의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절 you possess를 이끌어 명 사절을 이루므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 적절하다. (C) 사역동사 have의 동명사 형태인 having과 목적어인 명사구 the goal에 이어져 ‘have+목적어+목적격보어(~를 …하게 하다)’의 5형 식을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, 목적어인 the goal이 write(쓰다, 적다)의 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 written이 적절하다.

researching what essential skills, training or

to do next. Each path ⓑis unique and has different
challenges.

solution: 밑줄 친 ‘It reminds me of ~’는 ‘그것은 나에게 ~을 생각나게 한다’라는 뜻으로, 앞서 언급된 내용을 들은 뒤 떠오른 생각이 나 그와 관련된 경험에 대해 구체적인 예시를 덧붙일 때 사용 하는 표현이며, ‘It recalls ~(그것은 ~을 상기시킨다)’, ‘It brings to mind ~(그것은 ~을 마음속에 떠올리게 한다)’, ‘It makes me think of ~(그것은 나로 하여금 ~에 대해 생각하게 한다)’, ‘It serves as a reminder of ~(그것은 ~을 상기시켜 주 는 역할을 한다)’ 등으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있으나, ‘그것은 나에게 ~에 대해 알려준다’라는 의미로 어떤 것에 대한 정보를 알게 되었을 때 쓰는 표현인 ❷ ‘It informs me of ~’와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

body:
The history of food delivery in Korea goes back
(A)[very / much] further than one might imagine.
The earliest food delivered on record is
naengmyeon in the Joseon era. In his book, the
scholar Yunseok Hwang (1729-1791) mentions
(B)[that / what] he ordered naengmyeon for lunch
with his colleagues on the day after the state
examination in July 1768. It appears that
naengmyeon, a summer dish (C)[enjoying / enjoyed]
in the royal court, had gained popularity among
noblemen, leading to the introduction of delivery
services. In Yuwon Lee’s book, it is recorded that
King Sunjo (1790-1834) of Joseon ordered his
servants to buy naengmyeon and bring it back to
the palace so that he could eat it while looking at
the moon.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)           (B)
(C)
solution: (A) 부사 very는 원급을 강조할 때 쓰이므로, 비교급 형태의 부 사인 further를 수식할 수 없다. 따라서 ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 형 용사나 부사의 비교급을 강조하는 부사인 much가 알맞다. (B) mentions의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(he ordered ~ in July 1768)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어 가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. (C) that절의 동사로 had가 있으므로 ‘a summer dish ~ royal court’는 주어(naengmyeon)와 동사(had) 사이에 이중콤마로 삽 입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 동격의 명사구 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 a summer dish를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 형 태가 되어야 하며, a summer dish(여름철 요리)는 ‘즐겨지는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 enjoyed가 알맞다.

body:
A late Joseon dynasty scholar describes in his
book the delivery process of hyojonggaeng (soup
eaten with the early morning bells), which was
popular in the 1800s. He reports that famous
gukbap restaurants in Namhansanseong, Gyeonggi-do,
would prepare hyojonggaeng with meat, mushrooms,
and other vegetables, boil it, put it in a pot, and
deliver it to wealthy homes in Seoul early in the
morning. The hyojonggaeng remained (A)[warm /
warmly], having been delivered tightly wrapped in
cotton. This can be thought of as the first “early
morning delivery” in Korea, (B)[what / which] has
gained wide popularity in recent years. These days,
delivery service is available for every kind of food
imaginable, with options (C)[ranged / ranging] from
hamburgers to steak and even desserts. You don’t
have to go to a restaurant since food can be
delivered right to your home in less than an hour.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)          (C)
solution: (A) 동사 remain이 ‘(여전히) ~이다’를 뜻하는 2형식 동사로 쓰 였으며, remained에 이어지는 주격보어 자리에 부사는 쓰일 수 없으므로, 형용사인 warm(따뜻한)이 알맞다. (B) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(has ~ years)을 이 끌어 선행사인 early morning delivery를 부연 설명하는 관계 사절을 이루고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (C) 앞의 with, 명사 options와 함께 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’ 구문을 이루고 있으며, options(선택 들)가 ‘범위에 이르는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 ranging이 알맞다.

The history of food delivery in Korea goes back much further than one might imagine. The earliest food delivered on record is naengmyeon in the Joseon era. In his book, the scholar Yunseok Hwang (1729-1791) mentions that he ordered naengmyeon for lunch with his colleagues on the day after the state examination in July 1768. body:
Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be
carefully controlled, and a small mouth was
considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly
or mean. That’s why a serious expression was
common in most painted portraits, both in the East
and West. Even after the invention of photography,
the tradition continued.
The spread of cameras and camera companies’
advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early
photographers were not very good at getting
people to relax in front of the camera, so they
were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize
cameras, the companies tried to change this by
launching advertising campaigns that associated
photography with celebration. Companies wanted to
show customers that the camera was a tool for
capturing happy moments. They also found that
happy images helped their sales, so they began
using smiling models in their advertisements. Official
images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents
were smiling in their portraits.

emotional response in us. Artists use the same
color to express (C)[varied / identical] feelings, so
the way we interpret the artwork can be various
too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the
artwork come to you. You may love it or you may

beyond everyday life.

M: Mrs. Seo, I have a question about the last lesson.
W: What is it?
M: I noticed that Korean bills have a historical
figure on the front and a painting on the back.
Are the front and back related?
W: Yes. The historical figure on the front is
connected to the art on the back.
M: That’s interesting. So on the 5,000 won bill,
what does the painting on the back have to do
with the man on the front?
W: The man is Yi I, and the painting was done by
his mother.
M: She was a great artist! The plants look so real.
W: Many of my students have similar comments.
M: The house on the bill is beautiful, too. (A)I
wonder why it is drawn there.
W: It’s where he grew up. The mother and son are
honored by the bill’s design.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to
research, the French city of Arles, (A)[which / where]
van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally
bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed
the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt
there through bright yellow colors. During his short
life of 37 years, he created more than 900
paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly
yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers
(B)[include / includes] some of his most recognizable works.
Some have said that
his
preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a
medical condition that forced him (C)[seeing / to
see] mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can
also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors,
and these combinations of colors serve to
emphasize his joy being conveyed.
(A)
(B)          (C)
solution: (A) 쉼표 뒤에서 완전한 절(van Gogh spent his later years)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 선행사 the French city of Arles를 부 연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 계속적 용법의 관계 부사 where가 알맞다. (B) 주어부 ‘The series of paintings called Sunflowers’에 이어 진 문장의 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 series(연작)가 단수명사이므로, 이에 수일치시킨 단수동사 includes가 알맞다. (C) 과거형 동사 forced와 목적어 him에 이어져 ‘force+목적어 +목적격보어’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, force는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로 to see가 알맞다.

body:
Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward
Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper
lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and
he created paintings depicting urban scenes that
showed how even familiar surroundings could cause
the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s
Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are
four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly
not together. The bright yellow walls create a
dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, (A)어떻게
사람들이 같은 공간에 있으면서도 서로 떨어져 있다고
느낄 수 있는지를 강조합니다. In Hopper’s Automat,
the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The
yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat
of the woman, and the cool shades of the other
colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing
that she’s on her own.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Color is powerful because it stimulates (A)[a such /
such an] emotional response in us. Artists use the
same color to express various feelings, so the way
(B)[that / how] we interpret the artwork can be
various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions
of the artwork (C)[come / to come] to you. You
may love it or you may hate it, but art will always
take you to a place beyond everyday life.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 명사(구)를 수식하는 such(그러한)는 ‘such+(a/an+형용사+) 명사(구)’의 어순으로 쓰이므로, emotional response 앞에는 such an이 알맞다. (B) 완전한 절(we interpret the artwork)을 이끌어 선행사 the way를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 관계부사 자리이며, 관계 부사 how는 선행사인 the way와 함께 쓰이지 않으므로 관계 부사 대용의 that이 알맞다. (C) let과 목적어 the emotions of the artwork에 이어져 ‘let+ 목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리 로, 사역동사 let은 목적격보어로 동사원형을 취하는 동사이므 로 come이 알맞다. 비상(홍민표) 3과

body:
Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be
carefully controlled, and a small mouth was
considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly
or mean. That’s why a serious expression was
common in most painted portraits, both in the East
and West. Even after the invention of photography,
the tradition continued.
The spread of cameras and camera companies’
advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early
photographers were not very good at getting
people to relax in front of the camera, so they
were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize
cameras, the companies tried to change this by
launching advertising campaigns that associated
photography with celebration. Companies wanted to
show customers that the camera was a tool for
capturing happy moments. They also found that
happy images helped their sales, so they began
using smiling models in their advertisements. Official
images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents
were smiling in their portraits.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?

The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even
during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki
never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and
blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in
Korea, ⓐwhich inspired him to create paintings
ⓑfilled with various shades of blue. His use of blue
was an expression of how much he missed ⓒthe
place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310,
the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring
up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said
that he painted each dot as he thought of friends
and loved ones from home.
On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of
freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea
are two Matisse works that have an interesting
similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer
surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint
in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created
artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting
details. Although his physical difficulties prevented
him from doing many things, he still remembered
ⓓthe freedom he experienced while swimming in
the Tahitian sea, ⓔlooking through the salt water
down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
choices: ⓒ: the place which he grew up
solution: 명사구 the place를 선행사로 하는 목적격 관계대명사 which [that]가 생략된 채로 전치사 in의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져 있으므로, 전치사 in을 the place 뒤로 이동시킬 경우 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태의 in which로 전환해야 한다. 참고 로, in which를 장소의 관계부사 where로 바꿔 쓸 수도 있다.

happen?

body:
Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be
carefully controlled, and a small mouth was
considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly
or mean. That’s why a serious expression was
common in most painted portraits, both in the East
and West. Even after the invention of photography,
the tradition continued.
The spread of cameras and camera companies’
advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early
photographers were not very good at getting
people to relax in front of the camera, so they
were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize
cameras, the companies tried to change this by
launching advertising campaigns that associated
photography with celebration. Companies wanted to
show customers that the camera was a tool for
capturing happy moments. They also found that
happy images helped their sales, so they began
using smiling models in their advertisements. Official
images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents
were smiling in their portraits.

shift from serious expressions to smiling facesin photography

M: I noticed that Korean bills have a historical
figure on the front and a painting on the back.
Are the front and back related?
W: Yes. The historical figure on the front is
connected to the art on the back.
M: That’s interesting. So on the 5,000 won bill,
what does the painting on the back have to do
with the man on the front?
W: The man is Yi I, and the painting was done by
his mother.
M: She was a great artist! The plants look so real.
W: Many of my students have similar comments.
M: The house on the bill is beautiful, too. (A)I
wonder why it is drawn there.
W: It’s where he grew up. The mother and son are
honored by the bill’s design.

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward

lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and
he created paintings depicting urban scenes that
showed how even familiar surroundings could cause
the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness.
(A) The bright yellow walls create a dramatic
contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing
how people can be in the same space and feel
apart.
(B) Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this.
There are four people in the same diner, but
they’re clearly not together.

viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman,

with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on
her own.

body:
Our last color is red, which is often associated
with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the
Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the
same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The
painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground,
deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress
resembles a huge mountain against the background
of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the
relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red
㉠_______________________________________________. Claude
Monet’s Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the
artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The
bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing
and transformative power of nature. The painting
captures the dramatic moment when the forest
turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of
the river.
Color is powerful because it stimulates such an
emotional response in us. Artists use the same
color to express various feelings, so the way we
interpret the artwork can be various too. Open
your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork
come to you. You may love it or you may hate
it, but art will always take you to a place beyond
everyday life.

choices: is seen as a warning color in daily life
is used to express the beauty of nature
shows the way artists distance themselves from nature
is considered a particularly difficult color for artists to handle in art
solution:
① 빈칸 뒤에서 모네의 「아르장퇴유의 가을 효과」는 아름다운 가을의 순간을 기린 작품이며, 밝은 빨강이 자연의 놀랍고 변화시키는 힘을 상징한다고 했다.
② 따라서 빨강은 생명·에너지뿐 아니라 때로 '자연의 아름다움을 표현하는 데 쓰인다'는 내용이 알맞다.
③ ①·③·⑤는 뒤의 예시와 관련이 없고, ④는 자연과 거리를 둔다는 뜻이라 반대이다.
따라서 답은 ②이다.

Asteroid Mining
The solar system is composed of many rocks
floating in space. The large ones are called planets,
and the smaller ones are called asteroids. Research
has shown that asteroids (A)[contain / lack] valuable
resources like gold and rare earth elements. For
example, one asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported to
consist mainly of gold and other precious metals,
whose value is equal to billions of dollars per
person on Earth. From a space explorers’
perspective, however, the most valuable resources
from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals
nor rare mineral deposits. That valuable resource
could actually be water, and it seems to have been
(B)[valued / overlooked] because it doesn’t seem as
exciting as gold. Water is (C)[cheap / expensive] to
transport into space due to its weight and volume.
Having a space station with ⓐ________________________
________________________________ in orbit around Earth
would make space explorations much easier.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 소행성 16 프시케는 주로 금과 다른 귀금속으로 구성되어 있다는 예가 이어지므로, 연구에 따르면 소행성들은 금과 희토 류 원소와 같은 가치가 큰 자원을 포함하고 있다는 흐름이 알 맞다. 따라서 contain(~을 포함한다)이 적절하다. (B) 물은 금만큼 흥미진진해 보이지 않기 때문이라는 내용이 이어지므로, 물이 그런 이유로 간과되었다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 overlooked(간과되는)가 알맞다. (C) 물의 무게와 부피 때문이라는 내용이 이어지므로, 우주로 운송 하는 데 비용이 많이 든다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 expensive(비 싼)가 알맞다.

body:
M: Look at these photos taken by the Mars rovers.
W: Wow, Mars is so dusty and rocky.
M: Yes, it’s a very different environment from Earth.
That’s why people call it the Red Planet.
W: Hey, take a look at this picture. Is this the view
of the moon from Mars?
M: (A)I don’t think so. That’s probably the sunset
on Mars.
W: Are you sure? Why does the sun appear to be
so blue?
M: The Martian atmosphere contains more dust
particles than Earth, so the sunset appears blue.
W: That’s amazing. I would like to see it for myself.
M: Why not? Become an astronaut and maybe you
will.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: I don't think that's the case.
solution: 'I don't think so.'는 '그런 것 같지 않아.'라는 뜻으로, 사진에 보이는 것이 화성에서 본 달의 모습이냐는 질문에 대한 부정 적인 대답이므로, 상대의 의견에 대한 동의를 나타내는 ❸ ’네 말에 동의해.‘로 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

body:
No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will
look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most
(A)[likely / unlikely]. Robots will be sent to dig for
target materials and send them back towards Earth.
They will be programmed to explore the surface
and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks
such as drilling, collecting, and transporting. They
may work (B)[dependently / independently] or be
controlled remotely from Earth. Unfortunately, these
types of robots have yet to be developed since the
technology is still young. As technology continues
to (C)[advance / deteriorate], better methods for
obtaining materials will undoubtedly emerge.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 로봇들이 목표 물질들을 채굴해서 그것들을 지구에 보내기 위해 파견될 것이라는 내용이 이어지므로, 소행성 채굴의 방식 은 로봇 채굴이 가장 가능성이 높은 것 같다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 likely(가능성 있는)가 알맞다. (B) or(또는) 뒤에 지구에서 원격으로 제어될 수 있다는 또 다른 발전된 로봇 기술의 예시가 이어지므로, 로봇을 지칭하는 They(그 것들)가 독립적으로 작동할 수도 있다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 independently(독립적으로)가 알맞다. (C) 물질을 얻는 더 나은 방법은 의심할 여지 없이 등장할 것 이라는 내용이 이어지므로, As(~함에 따라)로 연결되는 내용은 기술이 계속 발전한다는 흐름이 되는 것이 적절하다. 따라서 advance(진보하다, 발전하다)가 알맞다.

body:
M: Hey, have you heard about artificial trees?
W: Artificial trees? No. What are those?
M: They’re structures designed to capture carbon
dioxide from the air, like real trees.
W: Incredible! How do they work?
M: They use various methods, but the most common
method is to use a special device to separate
the carbon dioxide from the surrounding air.
W: So, (A)is it likely that they’ll be able to help
solve the problem with the climate?
M: Some say so, but using artificial trees may not
be the best solution for the problem.
W: Why not?
M: It’s because they require a lot of energy for
operation and maintenance.
W: I see. I guess we have to consider the costs and
benefits of any technology.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: are they likely to help solve the climate problem
is it possible for them to help solve the climateproblem
are they necessary to help solve the climate problem
is there a chance that they’ll be able to help solvethe climate problem
is it probable that they will be able to help solvethe climate problem
solution: 어떤 상황이나 계획이 일어나거나 이루어질 가능성을 묻는 표현인 ‘is it likely that ~?(~할 가능성이 있니?)’을 사용하여 ‘그것들(=인 조 나무들)이 기후 문제를 해결하는 데 도움을 줄 가능성이 있니’ 라고 묻는 흐름이므로, 필요성의 여부를 묻는 ❸ ‘그것들이 기후 문제를 해결하는 것을 돕는 데 필요하니’와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

body:
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Creating good conditions for certain types of
manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of
energy and resources, but those conditions occur
naturally in space. Drugs, beauty and food products,
and advanced materials are all potential candidates
to be tested and produced in space. For example,
without the effects of gravity, products that require
a uniform quality like cosmetics would be (A)[easier
/ more difficult] to mix. Other materials like 3D
printed skin or muscle benefit from low pressure
and gravity too. Although the sun’s radiation can
be unhealthy for our skin, getting away from the
protective effects of the atmosphere could also
(B)[help / harm] the testing of products. For
example, fabrics and skin creams could be tested
for their ability to protect against solar radiation. Also, semiconductors and glass communication
cables could be produced with (C)[lower / higher]
purity and fewer faults.
solution:
① (A) 지구에서 만들기 어려운 조건이 우주에서는 저절로 생긴다고 했으므로, 중력이 없으면 균일한 품질이 필요한 화장품을 섞기가 '더 쉬울(easier)' 것이다.
② (B) Although로 '태양 복사는 피부에 해로울 수 있지만'과 대조되므로, 대기의 보호에서 벗어나는 것이 제품 시험에는 '도움이 될(help)' 수 있다.
③ (C) and fewer faults(더 적은 결함)와 나란하므로 '더 높은(higher)' 순도가 알맞다.
따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
The solar system is composed of many rocks
floating in space. The large ones are called planets,
and the smaller ones are called asteroids. Research
has shown that asteroids contain valuable resources
like gold and rare earth elements. For example, one
asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported ⓐ[consisting / to
consist] mainly of gold and other precious metals,
whose value is equal to billions of dollars per
person on Earth. From a space explorers’
perspective, however, the most valuable resources
from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals
nor rare mineral deposits. That valuable resource
could actually be water, and it seems to have been
overlooked because it doesn’t seem as exciting as
gold. Water is expensive to transport into space
due to its weight and volume. Having a space
station with sufficient water supplies in orbit around

that the cost of running a space program and
improving it has decreased substantially since
ambitious entrepreneurs have joined the adventure.
The conditions in space open up the possibility of
manufacturing newer and better products. Challenges
remain, but (A)it’s not unreasonable to imagine
sending a message from a device equipped with
semiconductors that were produced in space. The
space project will ultimately reach a point where
adventurous minds and their technological innovations
will be able to travel safely to stars beyond the solar
system. The resources required to drive economic
activity that have existed far beyond the reach of
humanity are becoming much more reachable. The
question is no longer about how; it’s about when.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Since the beginning of the space age in the
1950s, thousands of rockets and satellites have
been launched into space. Most have functioned as
they were designed to, but over time, some
machines have broken down and remain floating
around in space because they are difficult to bring
back. Dead satellites, used rocket parts, and small
pieces of dirt are in orbit. Those objects left
unattended in space are collectively referred to as
space junk. The presence of space junk _____________
__________________________________________________________.
For example, small pieces of junk might not seem
like a big issue, but they move at 6.7 kilometers
per second. At that speed, even a small piece of
metal can seriously harm satellites that provide
services across the world. In addition, each crash
has the potential to generate more space junk.
Without active efforts to remove the junk, traveling
in space would be extremely dangerous.
choices: creates opportunities for recycling materials inspace
greatly helps scientists understand how gravityworks
significantly increases risks to space activities andthe safety of astronauts
makes space agencies and companies carefullyconsider launching new satellites
solution: 작은 쓰레기 조각이라도 초당 6.7km의 속도로 움직이며 전 세 계에 서비스를 제공하는 위성에 심각한 피해를 줄 수 있다는 예가 이어지므로, 우주 쓰레기의 존재는 우주 활동에 위협이 된 다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ❹ ‘우주 활동과 우주비행사 의 안전에 대한 위험을 상당히 증가시킨다’가 빈칸에 알맞다.

body:
M: Hey, have you heard about artificial trees?
W: Artificial trees? No. What are those?
M: They’re structures designed to capture carbon
dioxide from the air, like real trees.
W: Incredible! How do they work?
M: They use various methods, but the most common
method is to use a special device to separate
the carbon dioxide from the surrounding air.
W: So, (A)is it likely that they’ll be able to help
solve the problem with the climate?
M: Some say so, but using artificial trees may not
be the best solution for the problem.
W: Why not?
M: It’s because they require a lot of energy for
operation and maintenance.
W: I see. I guess we have to consider the costs and
benefits of any technology.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Creating good conditions for certain types of
manufacturing on Earth requires the use of a lot of
energy and resources, but those conditions occur
naturally in space.
(A) For example, fabrics and skin creams could be
tested for their ability to protect against solar
radiation. Also, semiconductors and glass
communication cables could be produced with
higher purity and fewer faults.
(B) Other materials like 3D printed skin or muscle
benefit from low pressure and gravity too.
Although the sun’s radiation can be unhealthy
for our skin, getting away from the protective
effects of the atmosphere could also benefit the
testing of products.
(C) Drugs, beauty and food products, and advanced
materials are all potential candidates to be tested
and produced in space. For example, without the
effects of gravity, products that require a uniform
quality like cosmetics would be easier to mix.
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body: Which is true according to the passage? The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed.
choices: Van Gogh spent his later years in Arles, a city known for its exceptionally bright sunlight.
Van Gogh lived to be more than 50 years old.
Almost all of Van Gogh's paintings feature mostly yellow.
Van Gogh only used yellow in his artwork, avoiding all other colors.
Van Gogh's medical condition has been proven to be the sole reason for his use of yellow.
solution: ① 아를이 예외적으로 밝고 강렬한 햇빛을 지닌 도시였고 반 고흐가 그곳에서 말년을 보냈다는 내용이 본문에 명시되므로 일치한다. ② 37년의 짧은 생애를 살았다고 했으므로 50세 이상 살았다는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ③ 900점 이상의 작품 중 약 300점이 주로 노란색을 띤다고 했으므로 '거의 전부' 라는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ④ 파랑, 주황 등 다른 색도 함께 사용했다고 했으므로 노란색만 사용했다는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 의학적 상태는 '그렇게 말하는 사람들도 있다(Some have said)'는 하나의 견해로 제시될 뿐 입증된 사실이 아니므로 일치하지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 첫 문장에 쓰인 While과 쓰임이 같은 것을 <보 기>에서 고른 것은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show.
보기 ⓐWhile he was waiting for the bus, he read a book on his phone.
ⓑWhile some students prefer studying alone, others prefer studying in groups.
ⓒShe stayed calm while everyone else panicked during the fire drill.
ⓓWhile I was walking home, it suddenly started to rain.
ⓔWhile my dad was watching TV, my friends came to my house to play together.
solution: 지문의 While은 '~하는 반면에'라는 의미로, 독특한 색을 혼합해 쓰는 화가와 원색을 사용해 강한 감정을 표현하는 화가를 대조적으로 제시하는 접속사이다. ⓑ 혼자 공부하는 것을 선호하는 학생과 그룹으로 공부하는 것을 선호하는 학생을 대조하는 '반면에~'라는 뜻으로 쓰임이 같다. ⓒ 화재 훈련 중 침착했던 그녀와 당황했던 다른 사람들을 대조하는 '반면에~'라는 뜻으로 쓰임이 같다. 따라서, 정답은 ②가 가장 알맞다. ⓐ 버스를 기다리며 책을 읽었다는 동일 주어의 동시 동작을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓒ 대조의 의미로 알맞으나, ⓔ의 While은 코치가 영상을 검토하는 동안 선수들이 스트레칭을 했다는 단순한 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓓ 집으로 걸어가는 동안 비가 내리기 시작했다는 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이다. ⓔ '우리 아빠가 TV를 보시는 동안에, 친구들이 놀러 우리집에 왔다' 라는 의미로 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에' 라는 의미이다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
choices: Kim Whanki lost his Korean identity while living abroad in Paris and New York.
Kim Whanki's use of blue was connected to his longing for his hometown, Sinan.
Matisse painted Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea while standing at an easel.
Matisse's cancer surgery had no effect on his artistic method.
Matisse's later works show no connection to his personal memories.

solution: ⓐ where → which where는 이미 '전치사 + 관계대명사(in which)'의 의미를 포함하므로, 뒤에 다시 전치사 in을 쓰면 전치사가 중복된다. where 대신 which를 써야 알맞다. ⓒ which feature mostly yellow → of which feature mostly yellow '300 of the paintings feature mostly yellow(그 그림들 중 300점은 주로 노란색을 띤다)'에서 the paintings를 관계대명사로 바꾼 계속적 용법 구문이다. 이때 300은 전체 그림(paintings) 중 일부를 나타내는 수량표현이므로 반드시 전치사 of와 함께 써야 알맞다. 따라서, 정답은 ①, ③이 가장 알맞다. ⓑ '37년의 짧은 생애 동안'이라는 특정 기간을 나타내므로 전치사 During의 쓰임은 적절하다. ⓓ 노란색 선호가 특정 의학적 상태 '때문'이라는 인과관계를 나타내므로 전치사구 due to의 쓰임은 적절하다. ⓔ serve는 'serve to + 동사원형(~하는 역할을 하다, ~하는 데 도움이 되다)' 구문을 취하는 동사이다. 여기서는 파랑, 주황 등 다양한 색의 조합이 반 고흐가 느꼈던 삶의 기쁨을 강조하는 '역할을 한다, 기능을 한다'는 의미를 나타내야 하므로 어법상 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, ⓐknowing as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night,
ⓑsuggested the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows ⓒhow the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest
ⓓturned bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork ⓔto come to you. You may love it or you may hate it, but art will always take you to a place beyond everyday life.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments.에서 'shows'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 how가 쓰였다. 'how + 주어 + 동사'의 간접의문문 구조로, 동사 shows의 목적어절을 올바르게 이끌고 있어 어법상 옳다. 학생들이 what이나 that으로 혼동하기 쉽지만, '어떻게 화가가 아름다운 가을의 순간들을 기렸는지'라는 방법의 의미로 how가 적절하다. ① knowing as → known as R.C. Gorman은 '피카소로 알려진' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 주어(R.C. Gorman)와 분사의 관계가 수동(~로 알려진)이므로 현재분사 knowing이 아닌 과거분사 known을 써야 한다. 'be known as'의 수동 관계에서 비롯된 과거분사구문이어야 하므로 knowing as를 known as로 고쳐야 한다. ② suggested → suggesting 문장의 주어인 'Her figure in a red dress'가 능동적으로 '암시하는' 행위를 하는 것이므로 능동의 분사구문이 필요하다. 과거분사 suggested는 수동의 의미(~되어진)를 나타내므로 문맥과 맞지 않는다. 능동의 현재분사 suggesting으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ turned → turns 이 문장은 그림이 묘사하는 내용을 현재시제로 서술하는 문맥이다. 같은 절 내 'is reflected'가 현재시제로 쓰여 있고, 앞 문장들도 현재시제로 일관되게 서술하고 있으므로, when절의 동사도 현재시제 turns로 써야 한다. 과거시제 turned는 이 문맥에서 어법상 적절하지 않다. ⑤ to come → come 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)을 취한다. 'let + 목적어 + 동사원형'의 구조이므로, to come이 아닌 원형부정사 come을 써야 한다.
