body:
다음은 두 예술가의 파랑 색 쓰임을 비교 분석한 원문을 재 구성한 것이다. 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓔ에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 각각 영작하시오.
Kim Whanki & Henri Matisse The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut- outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky. While Kim Whanki's blue speaks of nostalgia for his homeland, Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Whanki, who lived abroad in Paris and New York, never forgot Korea; the blue sky and sea ⓐ him of his hometown, Sinan, inspiring paintings such as Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310, in which each dot ⓑ _____ as he thought of loved ones back home. Matisse, ⓒ cancer surgery in his later years, was ⓓ from standing and painting at an easel. Yet through works like Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea, he ⓔ _____ the sense of freedom he had once felt swimming in the Tahitian sea.
조건 1. ⓐ remind를 과거시제 능동태로 1단어로 쓸것
2. ⓑ paint를 수동태 과거시제로 2단어로 쓸 것
3. ⓒ have를 분사구문(완료형)으로 2단어로 쓸것
4. ⓓ prevent를 과거분사형으로 1단어로 쓸 것
5. ⓔ recall을 과거시제로 1단어로 쓸 것
보기 remind / paint / have / prevent / recall
ⓐ _____
ⓑ _____
ⓒ _____
ⓓ _____
ⓔ _____ 1회차 실전 모의고사
answer: ⓐ reminded ⓑ was painted ⓒ Having had ⓓ prevented ⓔ recalled
solution: ⓐ 파란 하늘과 바다가 그에게 고향을 '떠올리게 했다'는 과거 시점의 능동적 동작이므로 remind를 과거시제로 바꾸어 reminded로 쓴다. ⓑ 주어가 each dot(각 점)이므로, 그가 점을 '그렸다'는 원문의 능동 표현을 점이 '그려졌다'는 수동태로 전환하여 paint를 was painted로 쓴다. ⓒ 암 수술을 받은 것이 이후 상태(서서 그림을 그릴 수 없게 됨)보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로,have를 완료형 분사구문으로 바꾸어 Having had로 쓴다. ⓓ 주어 Matisse가 '~하지 못하게 되었다'는 수동의 의미이므로, was 뒤에 prevent를 과거분사형으로 바꾸어 prevented로 쓴다. ⓔ 그가 타히티 바다에서 느꼈던 자유를 '떠올렸다'는 과거 시점의 동작이므로 recall을 과거시제로 바꾸어 recalled로 쓴다.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. 1회차 실전 모의고사 The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration.
Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
choices: 1910년대 졸업앨범 사진 속 사람들은 카메라를 불편하게 여 겼을 것이다.
과거에는 동양보다 서양에서 큰 미소를 더 긍정적으로 바라 봤을 것이다.
카메라 회사들의 광고는 사진을 일상의 기록보다 축제와 연 결 짓는 방향이었을 것이다.
1950년대 이후 대통령들은 공식 초상화 촬영을 거부하게 되었을 것이다.
광고 속 미소 짓는 모델의 등장은 카메라 판매량 감소로 이 어졌을 것이다.
solution: ③ 카메라 회사들이 사진을 축제와 연결 짓는 광고 캠페인을 시작했다는 내용에서, 광고의 방향이 일상 기록보다 특별한 축하 순간을 강조하는 것이었음을 추론할 수 있다. ① 초기 사진사들이 사람들을 카메라 앞에서 편안하게 만드는 것을 잘 못했다는 내용은 있으나, 1910년대 졸업앨범 사진 속 인물들이 카메라를 불편하게 여겼다는 것은 본문에서 직접 추론할 수 없다. ② 큰 미소가 어리석거나 못된 것으로 여겨졌다는 것은 동서양 모두에 해당하는 내용으로, 동양과 서양 사이의 차이는 언급되지 않았다. ④ 1950년대에 대통령들이 초상화에서 미소를 짓기 시작했다는 내용이 있으므로, 공식 촬영을 거부했다는 추론은 본문과 모순된다. ⑤ 미소 짓는 모델의 사용이 판매에 도움이 되었다고 했으므로, 판매량 감소로 이어졌다는 추론은 본문과 정반대이다.

글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어가기에 어법상 알맞은 것은?
solution: (A) cause + 목적어 + to부정사 형태이므로 “cause the viewer to feel”이 올바르다. 따라서 to feel이 적절하다. (B) feel은 감각동사로 뒤에 형용사가 보어로 온다. apart는 ‘떨어져 있는, 분리된’이라는 형용사 역할을 할 수 있으므로 적절하다. 반면 apartly는 쓰이지 않는 형태이다. (C) 비교급 more를 강조할 때는 far, much, even 등이 사용된다. 따라서 “far more direct”가 자연스럽다. very는 원급 강조에 주로 쓰이며 비교급 more 앞에서는 사용할 수 없다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
Colorful Stories of Art Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show.
choices: primary: more important than anything else; basic and main
emotion: a strong feeling such as happiness, sadness, or anger
exhibition: a public display of works of art
explore: to examine or learn about something carefully
inspiration: a dark feeling of fear and worry caused by colors
solution: ⑤의 영영 풀이가 글의 내용 및 어휘의 실제 의미와 일치하지 않는다. inspiration은 ‘영감, 창조적인 생각이나 자극을 주는 것’을 의미한다. 본문에서도 “the three primary colors … were a source of inspiration”이라고 하여, 색깔들이 예술가들에게 창작의 동기와 아이디어를 제공했다는 의미로 사용되었다. 반면 제시된 풀이인 “a dark feeling of fear and worry caused by colors”는 ‘두려움이나 불안’에 관한 의미이므로 inspiration의 뜻으로 적절하지 않다. 나머지 선택지의 뜻 : ① primary: 주된, 기본적인 ② emotion: 감정 ③ exhibition: 전시회 ④ explore: 탐구하다, 자세히 살펴보다

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
choices: The calming influence of the color blue in daily life
Different meanings of blue expressed by two artists
How Matisse overcame physical difficulties through art
Kim Whanki's use of dots inspired by Sinan's landscape
The role of paper cut-outs in modern abstract painting
solution: ②가 정답이다. 글은 Kim Whanki의 파란색이 고향에 대한 그리움을 담고 있으며, Matisse의 파란색은 자유를 표현한다고 설명하고 있으므로, 두 화가가 파란색에 부여한 서로 다른 의미가 글의 주제로 가장 적절하다. ① 파란색이 일상에서 안정감을 준다는 내용은 도입부의 한 문장으로만 언급될 뿐, 글 전체의 주제를 포괄하지 못한다. ③ Matisse가 신체적 어려움을 극복한 방식은 Matisse를 소개하는 일부 사례일 뿐, 글의 핵심 주제는 아니다. ④ Sinan의 풍경에서 영감을 받은 점은 Kim Whanki의 점 기법을 설명하기 위한 세부 사항일 뿐, 글 전체 주제를 담지 못한다. ⑤ 종이 오리기 기법은 Matisse의 신체 상황을 설명하는 부수적 내용으로, 글의 중심 주제와 거리가 멀다.

The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was (B)
그가 주로 노란색으로만 보이게 되는 의학적 상태 때문이다 . While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to _____ .

(A)와 (B)를 각각 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오
조건 1. (A) 접속사 대신 전치사와 관계대명사를 사용할 것. create, than, feature를 포함할 것.
2. (B) 접속사 대신 전치사와 관계대명사를 사용할 것. medical, force, due를 포함할 것.
→
answer: (A) he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow (B) due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow
solution: 접속사 없이 두 문장을 연결하기 위해 전치사와 관계대명사를 활용해야 하므로, 정답은 (A) he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow, (B) due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow이다.

solution: ⓑ what → how "find out" 뒤에 이어지는 절 "they were a source of inspiration"은 주어(they)와 동사(were), 보어(a source of inspiration)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장 구조이다. 따라서 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 '어떻게 ~였는지'의 의미를 나타내는 how가 적절하다. what은 명사절 안에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데, 뒤 절이 이미 완전하므로 what은 올 수 없다. ⓓ conveying → being conveyed "his joy"는 색깔들의 조합에 의해 '전달되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 따라서 능동형 현재분사 conveying이 아니라 수동의 의미를 가진 being conveyed가 올바르다. ⓐ "unique"는 앞의 형용사 "interesting"과 병렬 구조를 이루며 명사 "colors"를 수식하는 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ "of which"는 선행사 "900 paintings" 중 일부인 "300"을 나타내는 [수사 + of which] 구조의 관계대명사구로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ "depicting"은 앞의 명사 "paintings"를 수식하는 현재분사로, paintings가 능동적으로 도시 장면을 묘사하는 주체이므로 올바르게 쓰였다.

We take ⓐit for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles ⓑwe flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles ⓒphotographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They ⓓmeasured each person’s smile ⓔby comparing the shape of their mouths. ④ ⓓ는 문장의 주어 A team의 술어 동사이다.
⑤ ⓔ는 measured를 수식하는 to부정사구이다.
solution: ①ⓐ it은 뒤에 이어지는 that절(that we should smile for the camera)을 진목적어로 하는 가목적어이므로 설명이 옳다. ② ⓑ we flash는 선행사 The smiles를 수식하는 관계대명사절이며, flash 뒤에 목적어가 없는 것으로 보아 목적격 관계대명사 that(또는 which)이 생략되어 있으므로 설명이 옳다. 따라서, 정답은 ①, ②가 가장 알맞다. ③ ⓒ photographed는 the smiles를 수식하는 과거분사이며, 문장의 동사가 아니므로 설명이 옳지 않다. ④ ⓓ measured는 주어 A team of computer scientists의 술어 동사가 아니라, 앞 문장의 analyzed에 이어 They(= A team of computer scientists)를 주어로 하는 별도 문장의 동사이므로 설명이 옳지 않다. ⑤ⓔ by comparing은 to부정사구가 아니라 '전치사 by + 동명사'로 이루어진 부사구이므로 설명이 옳지 않다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots
ⓐevoke images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties ⓑkept him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky. Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her ⓒimage in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and ⓓtransferable power of nature. The painting ⓔcaptures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
choices: 이 전시회는 primary colors 외에도 혼합색 작품을 중점 적으로 다룬다.
van Gogh는 Arles의 강렬한 햇빛을 경험하기 전부터 노 란색을 즐겨 사용했다.
van Gogh의 작품 중 노란색이 주로 사용된 그림은 600점 이상이었을 것이다.
Nighthawks 속 네 인물은 같은 공간에 있으면서도 서로 친밀한 관계이다.
Hopper의 Automat에서 따뜻한 노란색과 차가운 색조의 대비는 그림 속 여성의 고독감을 강조한다.
solution: ⑤ 본문은 Hopper의 Automat에서 노란 조명이 여성의 노란 모자로 시선을 유도하고, 다른 색들의 차가운 색조가 따뜻한 노란색과 대비를 이루어 여성이 혼자임을 강조한다고 설명한다. 이를 통해 따뜻한 노란색과 차가운 색조의 대비가 그림 속 여성의 고독감을 강조한다고 추론할 수 있다. ① 본문은 이 전시회가 세 가지 primary colors의 사용을 탐구한다고 했으므로, 혼합색 작품을 중점적으로 다룬다는 것은 추론할 수 없다. ② 본문은 van Gogh가 Arles에서 햇빛과 생명의 기쁨을 노란색으로 표현했다고만 서술하며, Arles 이전의 색채 선호에 대해서는 언급하지 않으므로 추론할 수 없다. ③ van Gogh가 900점 이상의 그림을 그렸고 그 중 약 300점이 주로 노란색을 사용했다고 명시되어 있으므로, 600점 이상이 노란색 위주라는 것은 사실과 다르다. ④ 본문은 Nighthawks 속 네 인물이 같은 식당에 있지만 명백히 함께가 아니라고 했으므로, 친밀한 관계라는 진술은 본문 내용과 모순된다.

The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, ⓐwhere van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he
ⓑfeeling there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 ⓒof which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings
ⓓcalling Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve ⓔto emphasize his joy being conveyed. _____ , _____ → _____ , _____ →
solution: ⓑ feeling → felt 관계대명사가 생략된 목적격 관계절 'he there'에서 동사가 필요하다. 문맥상 '그가 그곳에서 느꼈던 삶의 기쁨'이라는 의미이므로, 분사형 feeling이 아니라 과거 시제 동사 felt가 와야 한다. feeling은 이 자리에서 관계절의 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다. ⓓ calling → called 'The series of paintings'를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구이다. 'Sunflowers'라는 이름으로 불리는 것은 paintings이므로, paintings와 call의 관계는 수동(paintings are called Sunflowers)이다. 따라서 능동의 현재분사 calling이 아니라 수동의 과거분사 called가 와야 한다. ⓐ 'the French city of Arles'를 선행사로 하는 관계절에서 '반 고흐가 만년을 보낸 장소'라는 의미이므로, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'around 300 of which feature mostly yellow'는 「of which + 주어 + 동사」 구조의 관계절로, 선행사 '900 paintings' 중 300점을 가리킨다. 주어가 복수(300)이므로 동사 feature(복수 일치)도 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'serve to-부정사' 구조는 '~하는 역할을 하다'라는 의미의 관용 표현으로, to emphasize가 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
choices: the calming effects of various colors in modern art
different meanings of the color blue expressed by two artists
the influence of physical disabilities on artistic creation
traditional painting techniques of Kim Whanki and Henri Matisse
the history of paper cut-out art in the 20th century

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 '의학적 상태로 인한 노란색 선호'라는 주장을 언급한 방식으로 보아, 이에 대한 필자의 태도로 가 장 적절한 것은?
The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on her own.
choices: The writer firmly rejects the medical explanation as completely false.
The writer accepts the medical explanation while also pointing to evidence that suggests it is not the whole story.
The writer is indifferent to the debate and considers it irrelevant to understanding Van Gogh's art.
The writer strongly supports the medical explanation as the only valid interpretation of Van Gogh's use of yellow.
The writer criticizes art historians for ignoring the medical explanation entirely.
solution: ② 필자는 'While this may be true(이것이 사실일 수도 있지만)'라는 표현으로 의학적 설명의 가능성을 완전히 부정하지 않으면서도, 곧이어 그가 파랑, 주황 등 다른 색도 함께 사용해 기쁨을 강조했다는 근거를 제시하여 이 설명이 전부는 아니라는 여지를 남긴다. 따라서 정답은 ②가 가장 알맞다. ① 필자는 'may be true'라고 하여 의학적 설명의 가능성 자체를 완전히 배제하지 않으므로, 전면 부정한다는 내용은 알맞지 않다. ③ 필자는 이 논쟁에 대해 추가적인 근거(다른 색의 사용)를 제시하며 적극적으로 다루고 있으므로, '무관심 하다'는 내용은 알맞지 않다. ④ 필자는 다른 색의 사용을 근거로 의학적 설명이 유일한 해석이 아닐 수 있음을 시사하므로, '이를 유일하게 타당한 해석으로 강하게 지지한다'는 내용은 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 미술사학자들이 의학적 설명을 무시한다고 비판하는 내용은 본문에 전혀 없으므로 알맞지 않다.

Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. When you truly look at a painting, (A) _____ .

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times ⓐbigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile ⓑby comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth
ⓒis carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people ⓓto relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using ⓔsmiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③ is → be 'demanded that the mouth is carefully controlled'에서 demand는 요구·주장·제안을 나타내는 동사로, that절에 가정법 현재(동사원형)를 요구한다. 따라서 is를 동사원형 be로 고쳐야 한다. ① 'ten times bigger than'에서 배수 표현 뒤에 비교급 형용사 bigger가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'by comparing'은 전치사 by의 목적어로 동명사 comparing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 'get + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조로, get people to relax에서 to relax가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ smiling은 현재분사로서 명사 models를 앞에서 수식하는 형용사 역할을 하며 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
choices: to document the history of camera technology over time
to explain how social and commercial forces reshaped smiling norms in photos
to analyze the artistic standards of painted portraits in the East and West
to argue that yearbook portraits should reflect cultural identity

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times ⓐbiggest than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile ⓑby compare the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth
ⓒbe carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people ⓓto relaxing in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began ⓔused smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ 'demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled'에서 동사 demand는 당위적 의미를 나타내어 that절에 '(should +) 동사원형'을 요구하는 당위적 가정법을 취한다. 따라서 be가 원형동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ① biggest → bigger 배수 표현(ten times)과 함께 두 대상을 비교할 때는 반드시 비교급을 사용해야 한다. 최상급 biggest는 세 개 이상을 비교할 때 쓰이므로 비교급 bigger로 고쳐야 한다. ② by compare → by comparing 전치사 by 뒤에는 동사원형이 아닌 동명사(v-ing)가 와야 한다. 따라서 compare를 comparing으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ to relaxing → to relax get + 목적어 + to부정사 구조에서 목적격보어로는 'to + 동사원형'이 와야 한다. to 뒤에 동명사 relaxing을 쓸 수 없으므로 to relax로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ used → using began 뒤에는 동명사(v-ing) 또는 to부정사가 목적어로 올 수 있지만, 과거분사 used는 목적어 자리에 올 수 없다. 따라서 using으로 고쳐야 한다.

밑줄 친 우리말 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and 큰 미소는 어리석거나 못된 것 으로 여겨졌다. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued.
조건
1. be동사를 사용할 것
2. (viewed, silly, big smiles, as, or, mean)을 모두 포 함할 것
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것
→
answer: Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean.
solution: ~로 여겨지다'는 수동태 표현 'be viewed as'를 사용하여 나타낸다. 주어는 'Big smiles'이고, be동사는 주어의 수와 시제(과거)에 맞게 'were'로 쓴다. '어리석거나 못된'은 'silly or mean'으로 표현하며, 박스에 제공된 'viewed, silly, big smiles, as, or, mean'을 모두 활용하여 'Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean.'으로 완성한다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own. The two artists used the same color of yellow to create very different moods. While Van Gogh used yellow to express the (A) _____ he felt in Arles, Hopper used it to highlight urban (B) _____ . Some have claimed that the (C) _____ feature the color because of a medical condition. In contrast, with clear artistic intent, the (D) _____ the contrast between the warm yellow interior and the cold dark city outside in his paintings.

보기 make / latter / viewers / be / force / to / feel / former
(C) _____
(D) _____
answer: (C) former / was forced to (D) latter / made viewers feel
solution: (C) van Gogh의 작품군을 가리켜야 하고 수동의 의미를 지니므로, former was forced to가 적절하다. (D) Hopper를 가리켜야 하고, 사역동사 make가 쓰여야 하므로, latter made viewers feel이 적절하다.

solution: ② 본문은 노랑, 파랑, 빨강이라는 세 가지 원색이 영감의 원천이었음을 탐구하겠다고 예고하며 마무리된다. 이어지는 내용은 순서상 첫 번째 색인 노란색을 다룬 화가의 사례로 이어지는 것이 자연스러우므로, 정답은 ②가 가장 알맞다. ① 색을 섞어 새로운 색을 만드는 방법에 대한 구체적 설명은 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 전시회의 위치나 관람 시간과 같은 실용적 안내는 글의 흐름과 무관하므로 알맞지 않다. ④ 원색이 사용되지 않게 된 역사적 배경은 글의 취지(원색을 통한 영감 탐구)와 반대되므로 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 색채 이론을 연구한 과학자들에 대한 내용은 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors─yellow, blue, and red─and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show.
choices: exploring the use of primary colors in art
examining various ways to express emotions
understanding how colors influence our emotions
appreciating the beauty of colorful natural scenery
solution: 예술가들이 노란색, 파란색, 빨간색이라는 세 가지 삼원색을 어떻게 영감의 원천으로 사용했는지 전시회를 통해 탐구하는 내용의 글이다. 따라서 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ① ‘예술에서 삼원색의 사용 탐구하기’이다.

body: Which is the best title for the passage? The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. 실전 모의고사 4회차
choices: Van Gogh's Yellow: Painting the Joy of Sunlit Arles
The Tragic Illness Behind Van Gogh's Genius
Sunflowers: The Most Expensive Painting in History
Arles: A Travel Guide to Van Gogh's French Hometown
Van Gogh's Rivalry with Fellow Impressionist Painters
solution: ① 'Van Gogh의 노란색: 햇빛을 받은 아를의 기쁨을 그리다' 이라는 의미로 글의 핵심 내용을 압축적으로 담고 있으므로 정답으로 가장 알맞다. ② 의학적 상태는 글에서 하나의 가설로만 제시될 뿐 중심 소재가 아니므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 경매가에 대한 내용은 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ④ 여행 안내 형식의 제목은 글의 예술적 초점과 맞지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 다른 화가와의 경쟁 관계는 글에 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on her own.
choices: depict: to show or describe something in a picture or story
surroundings: the things and conditions around a person or place
contrast: a noticeable difference between two things
shade: a loud and powerful sound that fills a space
on one’s own: alone; without other people
solution: ④ shade는 ‘색조, 그늘’이라는 뜻으로, 본문에서는 “the cool shades of the other colors”에서 색의 다양한 톤이나 색조를 의미한다. 그러나 제시된 영영 풀이인 “a loud and powerful sound that fills a space”는 ‘크고 강한 소리’ 라는 뜻이므로 shade의 의미와 맞지 않는다. 반면 나머지 선택지는 모두 본문의 의미에 알맞다. ① depict: ‘묘사하다, 나타내다’ ② surroundings: ‘주변 환경’ ③ contrast: ‘대조, 뚜렷한 차이’ ⑤ on one’s own: ‘혼자서, 홀로’ 를 의미한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork come to you. You may love it or you may hate it, but art will always take you to a place beyond everyday life.

윗글에서 밑줄 친 take you to a place beyond everyday life가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Art helps viewers feel deeper emotions or imagine more freely.
Art leads viewers to thoughts that can be used in everyday situations.
Art encourages viewers to step away from their usual daily routines.
Art requires viewers to follow shared rules when finding meaning.
Art allows viewers to notice details they normally do not pay attention to.
solution: 예술은 우리의 일상을 넘어선 경험을 제공한다는 내용의 글이다. 이처럼 예술이 제공하는 특별한 경험을 나타내므로, 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은 ① ‘예술은 관람객들이 더 깊은 감정을 느끼거나 더 자유롭게 상상하도록 돕는다.’이다.

In the painting, three customers sit at the counter of an all-night diner. A lone man sits with his back turned to the outside world, while a man and a woman sit closely together as a couple across from him. The counter worker is standing inside, looking straight ahead.
choices: 서현준: 식당 안의 네 사람은 비록 물리적으로 같은 공간에 있지만, 서로 시선을 나누거나 소통하지 않는 단절된 상태에 있음을 유추할 수 있어.

강은혜: 어두운 외부 세계와 대비되는 식당 내부의 밝은 노란 색 벽은 그 안에 있는 인물들의 쓸쓸함과 분리된 감정을 더 강렬하게 부각해.
solution: 작품 Nighthawks에서 카운터 직원이 정면을 응시하고 인물들이 서로 소통하지 않는 묘사는 대도시 속 현대인들이 겪는 단절과 소외감을 시각적으로 극대화하기 위한 장치이다. 따라서 바르게 분석하지 못한 학생은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? 4회차 실전 모의고사 Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued.
The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that _____ . Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
choices: highlighted the technical skills of photographers
discouraged people from taking serious portraits
promoted the beauty of a small and controlled mouth
introduced smiling models to painted portrait traditions 유형보충독해1
solution: ① 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 카메라를 대중화하기 위해 회사들이 광고 캠페인을 시작했다는 내용이며, 바로 다음 문장에서 'Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments'라고 하여 사진을 축제·행복한 순간과 연결지으려 했음을 밝히고 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 광고 캠페인이 사진 촬영을 축하·기념과 연결시켰다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 'associated photography with celebration'이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 맞는 것은?
The Story of Smiling Selfies We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
choices: stone-faced: showing strong excitement or happiness on the face
analyze: to study something carefully in order to understand it
portrait: a picture of a natural place such as mountains or forests
popularize: to make something less known to people
advertisement: a private letter sent from one person to another 유형보충독해1
solution: ② analyze는 ‘분석하다, 자세히 조사하다’라는 뜻으로, 본문에서는 컴퓨터 과학자들이 37,000장이 넘는 졸업사진을 조사하고 미소의 형태를 비교했다는 내용에서 사용되었다. 따라서 “to study something carefully in order to understand it”이라는 영영 풀이가 알맞다. 반면 나머지 선택지는 어휘의 의미와 맞지 않는다. ① stone-faced는 ‘무표정한, 굳은 표정의’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘신나거나 행복한 표정의’라는 의미이므로 틀리다. ③ portrait는 ‘초상화, 인물 사진’인데, 제시된 풀이는 풍경화를 의미하므로 틀리다. ④ popularize는 ‘널리 알리다, 대중화하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘덜 알려지게 하다’이므로 반대 의미이다. ⑤ advertisement는 ‘광고’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘개인 편지’의 의미이므로 틀리다.

solution: ③ 사진 발명 이후에도 진지한 표정의 전통이 계속되었다고 명시되어 있으므로, 사진 기술이 발명 당시부터 회화와 다른 표정을 담아냈다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ① 작은 입과 진지한 표정이 과거의 기준이었다가 이후 미소가 표준이 되었다는 변화로 보아, 표정에 대한 사회적 기준이 시대에 따라 달라질 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다. ② 카메라 회사의 광고가 사람들의 표정(자기표현 방식)을 미소로 바꾸는 데 영향을 미쳤다는 내용으로 보아 추론할 수 있다. ④ 광고 속 미소가 결국 대통령의 공식 초상에도 반영되었다는 내용으로 보아, 대중적 변화가 공적 영역에도 영향을 줄 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 행복한 이미지가 판매에 도움이 되었다는 내용으로 보아, 긍정적 감정과 제품을 연결하는 전략이 소비자 행동에 영향을 줄 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다.

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A),
(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That’s why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies’ advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits. Portraits once favored (A) _____ expressions, but camera companies' advertising campaigns, which linked photography with happiness, gradually made (B) _____ expressions the new standard.
solution: 요약문은 초상화가 한때 (A) '진지한(serious)' 표정을 선호했으나, 사진을 행복과 연결시킨 카메라 회사들의 광고 캠페인이 점차 (B) '미소 짓는(smiling)' 표정을 새로운 표준으로 만들었다는 것을 설명한다. (A) 본문에서 'a serious expression was common in most painted portraits(대부분의 초상화에서 진지한 표정이 흔했다)'라고 했으므로, '진지한(serious)'이라는 표현이 들어가야 알맞다. (B) 본문에서 카메라 회사들이 사진을 행복과 연관 짓는 광고 캠페인을 통해 미소 짓는 모델을 광고에 사용하기 시작했고, 결국 1950년대에는 대통령들도 초상화에서 미소를 짓게 되었다고 했으므로, '미소 짓는(smiling)'이라는 표현이 들어가야 알맞다. 따라서, 정답은 ④ serious - smiling 이 가장 알맞다.

solution: (A)의 'it'은 앞의 단수명사 'this struggle'을 가리키므로 적절하다. (B)는 'have + 목적어 + 동사원형'의 사역동사 구조이므로 'keep'이 알맞다. (C)는 그 습관이 얼마나 비효율적인지 알아보기 위한 목적을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 'to see'가 알맞다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
A kangaroo's tail, ⓐthat is made up of over twenty vertebrae, acts as a powerful muscle for balance and movement. The tail works almost like a fifth leg ⓑso that the kangaroo can hop, turn, and even fight without losing stability. When a kangaroo stands still, its tail ⓒsupports most of its body weight while the legs rest. During a fight, a kangaroo often begins ⓓkicking its opponent with both hind legs while balancing on its tail. Before hopping away, the kangaroo tucks its front legs close to its chest to protect ⓔthem from injury. *vertebrae: 척추뼈
solution: ①ⓐ이 정답이다. 'A kangaroo's tail, that is made up of over twenty vertebrae'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓒ 주어 'its tail'이 단수이므로 단수동사 'supports'가 알맞다. ⓓ 'begin + -ing' 구조에서 'kicking'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'front legs'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 밑줄 친 부분이 어법상 올바르면 O표, 틀리면 •표하고 바르게 고치시오.
India-born writer Priya Rao remembered her first days of working in the U.S. were stressful. While she was used to drafting all the scripts herself and having them (A)carry out faithfully, Priya Rao found that the American writing style allowed everyone
(B)have a voice.
(A) ( O / X )
(B) ( O / X )
solution: (A) 'scripts'는 수행되는 대상이므로 'carry'를 과거분사 'carried'로 고쳐야 한다. (B) 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조이므로 'have'를 'to have'로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 답은 (A) X, carried, (B) X, to have이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
She got her bike _____ at the repair shop after the accident.
solution: 'get+목적어+과거분사' 구조로, 목적어(자전거)가 수리되는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사가 와야 한다. 따라서 정답은 ①repaired이다. ②repair(원형), ③to repair(부정사), ④repairing(현재분사, 능동의 의미), ⑤repairs(3인칭단수형)는 모두 목적어와의 관계상 적절하지 않으므로 오답이다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
The belief that art can't convey scientific truth is such a rigid assumption that it is hard ⓐfor critics to challenge. This assumption is strong enough to make audiences ⓑ to dismiss artistic interpretations of science. A lot of scholars have this view because ⓒit is easier to separate art from science than to combine them. The insistence on strict boundaries conveniently allows institutions ⓓto maintain traditional curricula. Clearly, a new approach to education
ⓔis needed for interdisciplinary learning to thrive.
solution: ⓑ to dismiss → dismiss 사역동사 make는 「make + 목적어 + 동사원형」 구조를 취하므로 make audiences dismiss가 알맞다. ⓐ it은 앞의 assumption을 가리키며, for critics to challenge는 ‘비평가들이 그것에 이의를 제기하기에’라는 의미이므로 올바르다. ⓒ 「It is easier to separate A from B than to combine them」에서 it은 가주어이고, 뒤의 to부정사구가 진주어 역할을 하므로 올바르다. ⓓ allow + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 allows institutions to maintain은 올바르다. ⓔ 주어 a new approach가 단수이므로 is needed가 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Some years ago, a coach named Daniel Kim invited a group of nervous rookies to his gym and asked them (A)[perform / to perform] boldly while pretending to play in a championship game. He measured how bold they appeared based on their movements and facial expressions. He found that some of the nervous rookies did a strikingly convincing job of looking bold. Thus, this experiment shows that most of us seem to (B)
[know / be known] how to hide our nerves to some extent. Whether or not we're aware that the way we move reveals our nervousness, we control it (C)[automatic / automatically]. 실전 학습
solution: (A) ask + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to perform이 적절하다. (B) seem to + 동사원형 구조이며, 문맥상 ‘우리가 스스로 아는 것’이라는 능동의 의미이므로 know가 적절하다. be known은 ‘알려지다’라는 수동의 의미가 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. (C) 동사 control을 수식해야 하므로 부사 automatically가 적절하다. 형용사 automatic은 동사를 수식할 수 없다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분이 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: The audience was too polite to interrupt the speaker.
The security guard spotted the man climbing over the fence.
She seems to have forgotten our appointment.
The report to submit by Friday requires more data.
The director had the assistant to prepare the documents overnight.
solution: ⑤ to prepare → prepare 사역동사 have는 「have + 목적어 + 동사원형」 구조를 취하므로 had the assistant prepare가 알맞다. ① too + 형용사 + to부정사 구조로 올바르다. ② spot + 목적어 + 현재분사 구조로 올바르다. ③ to have forgotten은 주절의 시점보다 앞선 일을 나타내는 완료부정사로 올바르다. ④ to submit은 명사 the report를 뒤에서 수식하는 형용사적 용법으로 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
One way to make a defender (A)[struggle / struggling] harder is to change speed suddenly. For example, a striker running toward the goal slows down and speeds up repeatedly and forces the defender (B)[react / to react] quickly. Changing pace is easier for the striker than for the tired defender. The defender also cannot tell whether the striker will accelerate or slow down, so the defender cannot plan the next tackle. As a result, the striker makes the attack more (C)
[complicated / complicatedly] for the defender. Though the defender may still succeed in stopping the attack, there is a chance that the defender may lose balance and fall behind.
solution: (A) 사역동사 make는 목적어 뒤에 원형부정사를 목적격보어로 취하므로 'struggle'이 적절하다. (B) force는 목적어 뒤에 to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하므로 'to react'가 적절하다. (C) make의 목적격보어 자리이므로 형용사 'complicated'가 와야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 대화를 읽고 주어진 질문에 답하시오.
A: Jason, you ⓐmust have heard about the trip already, right?
B: Yeah, I noticed the suitcase ⓑlying by the door this morning.
A: But why do you look so ⓒnervously about it?
B: (A)그가 어제 나에게 여행 가방을 확인하게 하셨어. (make, check, the suitcase) I don't want to see him ⓓworry about it anymore.
A: That's understandable. But he also wants you
ⓔwaiting until tomorrow, doesn't he?

위 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것의 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
(1) _____ → (2) _____ →
solution: ⓒ nervously → nervous 감각동사 look 뒤에는 형용사가 와야 하므로 nervously를 nervous로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ waiting → to wait want + 목적어 + to부정사 구조를 취하므로 waiting을 to wait로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ must have heard는 조동사 + have + p.p. 구조로 과거에 대한 추측을 나타내므로 올바르다. ⓑ lying은 notice + 목적어 + 현재분사 구조로 진행 중인 동작을 나타내므로 올바르다. ⓓ worry는 지각동사 see가 see + 목적어 + 원형부정사 구조를 취하므로 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 대화를 읽고 주어진 질문에 답하시오.
A: Jason, you ⓐmust have heard about the trip already, right?
B: Yeah, I noticed the suitcase ⓑlying by the door this morning.
A: But why do you look so ⓒnervously about it?
B: (A)그가 어제 나에게 여행 가방을 확인하게 하셨어. (make, check, the suitcase) I don't want to see him ⓓworry about it anymore.
A: That's understandable. But he also wants you
ⓔwaiting until tomorrow, doesn't he?

위 대화의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)와 같도록 괄호 안의 말을 활용 하여 문장을 완성하시오.
→ _____ yesterday.
answer: He made me check the suitcase
solution: 사역동사 make는 'make+목적어+동사원형' 형태로 쓰여 '(목적어)가 ~하게 하다'라는 의미를 나타낸다. 따라서 make 뒤에 목적어 me와 동사원형 check를 이어서 쓴다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Warm milk helps babies fall asleep easily.
The teacher had the students submit their essays online.
The security guard noticed the man to enter the building without a badge.
They got the contract signed before the deadline.
The officer asked the driver to show his license.
solution: ③ to enter → enter 지각동사 notice는 목적어 + 원형부정사/현재분사의 형태를 취하므로 to enter를 enter로 고쳐야 한다. ① help + 목적어 + 원형부정사 형태로 fall이 알맞다. ② 사역동사 have는 목적어 + 원형부정사를 취하므로 submit이 알맞다. ④ get + 목적어 + 과거분사에서 the contract와 signed가 수동 관계이므로 알맞다. ⑤ ask + 목적어 + to부정사 형태로 to show가 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음을 읽고, 어법상 틀린 부분을 한 군데 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
Fast food consumption has had positive influences on the way people manage their busy schedules and save time. However, although fast food seems to make life more convenient, it is actually creating more health risks. The more often people eat fast food, the less balanced nutrition they get. Many doctors now believe that poor nutrition can lead to a number of physical problems. In fact, a recent study showed that fast food increases blood sugar levels, that explains why people who eat fast food regularly experience significant levels of obesity, diabetes, and other health issues.
→
solution: 콤마 뒤에서 앞에 나온 절 전체를 선행사로 받아 추가 설명을 덧붙이는 비제한적 관계대명사 자리에는 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 한다. 'increases blood sugar levels, that explains why'의 that을 which로 바꿔야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
어법상 틀린 것을 모두 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
ⓐDid you see the boy and his rabbit that were playing in the garden?
ⓑThis is all that matters to me now.
ⓒChoose that you feel is best for you.
ⓓShe is the only friend that supported me.
ⓔThe tool with that he built the table is gone.
→
→
answer: ⓒ that → what, ⓔ with that → with which
solution: ⓒ은 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 관계대명사 that을 명사절처럼 쓴 오류로, that을 what으로 고쳐야 한다. (Choose what you feel is best for you.) ⓔ는 관계대명사 that이 전치사 바로 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 with that을 with which로 고쳐야 한다. (The tool with which he built the table is gone.) ⓐ은 선행사가 사람(boy)과 동물(rabbit)이 함께 있을 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다. ⓑ는 all이 선행사일 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 적절하므로 옳다. ⓓ는 the only가 선행사를 수식할 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A)~(C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현을 골라 짝지은 것을 고르시오.
Noise-canceling technology allows headphones
(A)[is / to be] partially silent to surrounding sounds. It is important to note, however, that it does not perfectly block noise. The technology cannot make headphones completely silent; instead, it (B)[works / works as] a kind of sound barrier by reducing the volume of external noise that reaches the ears. Normally, noise-canceling technology is used to reduce the discomfort of loud environments during long flights. It is also used in busy offices to enable workers to concentrate without being disturbed by background noise. Although noise-canceling technology can help users (C)[focus / focused] on their tasks, some background sounds are still noticeable.
choices: is - works as - focused 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복
solution: (A)는 allow + 목적어 + to부정사의 구조이므로 to be가 와야 한다. (B)는 뒤에 명사구 a kind of sound barrier가 이어지므로 ‘~로서 기능하다’라는 뜻의 works as가 와야 한다. (C)는 help + 목적어 + 동사원형의 구조이므로 focus가 와야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Is space debris a danger or a resource for future missions? Actually, it is both. A cloud of debris could force satellites (A)[alter / to alter] their orbits suddenly, but old satellite parts also contain reusable metals and electronics. Now a startup called OrbitClean Ltd. wants (B)[remove / to remove] hazardous debris from low Earth orbit and recycle materials for new spacecraft. Engineers operating robotic arms from ground stations might do the removal, or an unmanned craft would first approach a piece of debris and secure it with a net, within a controlled distance. Meanwhile, the European Space Agency plans to send a cleanup satellite called ClearOrbit (C)
[capture / to capture] debris fragments in 2028. * debris 파편
choices: to alter - to remove - to capture
solution: (A) force + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to alter가 적절하다. (B) want + to부정사 구조이므로 to remove가 적절하다. (C) to capture는 청소 위성을 보내는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사이다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
The manager got Sarah _____ the report to the board.
solution: 사역동사 get은 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 to present가 와야 한다. Sarah가 보고서를 발표하는 주체이므로 능동형 to부정사가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다. present(②)와 presents(③)는 동사 형태로 get의 목적격 보어 자리에 쓸 수 없고, be presented(④)와 to be presented(⑤)는 수동형으로 문맥상 맞지 않는다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
It was early in the spring of 1893 that rumors of a bank failure did not spread ⓐgradually but seemed to appear everywhere at once. In those days, we had no radios ⓑto broadcast such news across the city. The city council soon held several sessions about steps ⓒto calm the public's fears. Nevertheless, the true state of the bank's finances was kept entirely ⓓsecret from ordinary depositors. It was only later that I heard a close friend ⓔto admit that he had withdrawn all his savings weeks before.
solution: 지각동사 heard의 목적격 보어 자리에는 원형부정사가 와야 하므로 to admit은 admit으로 고쳐야 한다. 나머지 밑줄 친 부분은 모두 어법상 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: When you skip drinking water, you are like an engine trying to run without oil. Experts say that proper hydration is the brain's coolant. Brains that are fully hydrated (A)[concentrate / to concentrate] better and react faster. Some students say that (B)[get / getting] a few extra minutes of a break is more important than drinking a glass of water, but they're wrong. Of course, taking breaks is important, but drinking water regularly would be better than ignoring thirst and skipping hydration. For students who want to do well in school, water is the most important resource of the day. Give your brain the fluid it needs to make it (C)[run / to run] well. To think more clearly and faster, drink plenty of water.
solution: 문장의 주어는 Brains이고 that are fully hydrated는 주어를 수식하는 관계절이므로 문장의 본동사가 필요하다. 따라서 (A)에는 원형 concentrate가 적절하다. that절의 주어 자리이므로 동명사가 필요하므로 (B)에는 getting이 적절하다. make는 사역동사로 목적격보어에 원형부정사를 취하므로 (C)에는 run이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ②이다. ① getting이 get으로 되어 있어 (B)가 틀리다. ③ to run은 run이 되어야 한다. ④ to concentrate는 concentrate가 되어야 하고 to run은 run이 되어야 한다. ⑤ to concentrate는 concentrate가 되어야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 적절 한 것은?
The first day of practice is your opportunity to present your vision of the season to new athletes. It is helpful if you can introduce yourself (A)[to them / them] as a coach and leader and provide insight into how you will train the team and what you will expect them (B)[achieve / to achieve] during the season. Consider that several of your athletes may be “trying out” for a position the first week of practice. They may be looking for a team that will fit a particular schedule or offer a particular training style (i.e. drill-based or scrimmage style). You may also want to model, as
(C)[specific / specifically] as possible, the team culture that you want to foster. Thus, athletes will appreciate a clear roadmap of what you will require of them over the course of the season.
solution: (A) introduce oneself to + 사람 구조이므로 to them이 적절하다. (B) expect + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to achieve가 적절하다. (C) 동사 model을 수식해야 하므로 부사 specifically가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 적절 한 것은?
When you skip exercise, you are like a phone trying to run without a charge. Experts say that regular exercise is the brain's power source. Brains that are regularly exercised (A)
[concentrate / to concentrate] better and solve problems faster. Some students say that (B)[get / getting] a few extra minutes of rest is more important than going for a quick run, but they're wrong. Of course, resting is important, but going for a short jog in the morning would be better than sleeping late and skipping exercise. For students who want to do well in school, exercise is the most important habit of the day. Give your brain the boost it needs to make it (C)[run / to run] well. To think more clearly and faster, get some exercise every day.
solution: 문장의 주어는 Brains이고 that are regularly exercised는 주어를 수식하는 관계절이므로 문장의 본동사가 필요하다. 따라서 (A)에는 원형 concentrate가 적절하다. that절의 주어 자리이므로 동명사가 필요하므로 (B)에는 getting이 적절하다. make는 사역동사로 목적격보어에 원형부정사를 취하므로 (C)에는 run이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ③이다. ① getting이 get이 되어 있어 (B)가 틀리다. ② to concentrate는 concentrate가 되어야 하고 to run은 run이 되어야 한다. ④ to concentrate는 concentrate가 되어야 하고 get은 getting이, to run은 run이 되어야 한다. ⑤ to concentrate는 concentrate가 되어야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 문장 형식이 다른 하나를 고르시오.
choices: The award made her incredibly proud.

Teachers help students understand difficult concepts.

They rescued the injured hikers by using ropes and ladders. 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: ⑤는 'rescued+목적어'로 목적어만 취하는 3형식 문장이며, 나머지는 모두 목적격보어를 동반하는 5형식 문장이다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
ⓐThe director made the film more _____ .
ⓑThe pianist played the piece _____ .

solution: ⓐ make+목적어+형용사 구조이므로 exciting이 적절하다. ⓑ played를 수식하는 것은 부사이므로 gently가 적절하다. ⓒ 지각동사 saw는 목적격보어로 원형부정사를 취하므로 arrange가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The coach watched the players _____ hard during the game.
• The owner found the vase _____ badly.
solution: 정답은 ③이다. 지각동사 watched는 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동관계일 때 현재분사(running)를 쓰고, find는 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동관계일 때 과거분사(broken)를 쓴다. 따라서 running - broken이 정답이다. ① to run은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없고, break는 the vase와 수동관계를 나타낼 수 없어 틀렸다. ② to run은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없어 틀렸다. ④ running은 맞지만 break는 원형으로 the vase와 수동관계를 나타낼 수 없어 틀렸다. ⑤ ran은 동사의 과거형이므로 목적격보어로 쓸 수 없어 틀렸다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
• The mother heard her son _____ in his room.
• The manager left the office overnight.
solution: 정답은 ①이다. 지각동사 heard는 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동관계일 때 현재분사(singing)를 목적격보어로 쓴다. leave는 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동관계일 때 과거분사 (locked)를 목적격보어로 쓴다. 따라서 singing - locked가 정답이다. ② to sing은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없어 틀렸고, lock은 목적어(the office)와 수동관계이므로 과거분사가 와야 한다. ③ to sing은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없고, locking은 the office와 능동관계가 아니라 수동관계이므로 틀렸다. ④ singing은 맞지만 lock은 원형으로 the office와 수동관계를 나타낼 수 없어 틀렸다. ⑤ sang은 동사의 과거형이므로 목적격보어로 쓸 수 없어 틀렸다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓒ 중 어법상 틀린 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
Since 1901, the Nobel Prize has evolved from a modest award into one of the most respected honors in the world. The Nobel Prize ceremony,
ⓐwhich takes place in Stockholm every December, draws attention from across the globe. Malala Yousafzai delivered the speech
ⓑthat inspired millions of young activists worldwide. The 2014 Peace Prize, ⓒthat was shared between Malala Yousafzai and Kailash Satyarthi, marked a historic moment for children's rights.
→
solution: ⓒ는 콤마 뒤에서 선행사 The 2014 Peace Prize에 추가 정보를 덧붙이는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사절이므로 that을 쓸 수 없고 which를 써야 한다. ⓐ의 which는 계속적 용법으로 올바르고, ⓑ의 that은 선행사 the speech를 수식하는 제한적 용법의 주격 관계대명사이므로 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 맞는 것을 고르시오.
choices: The man lives across the street fixed my car.
Jake is more careful than his brother is, which everyone appreciates.
This is the best restaurant what we have ever visited.
Could you explain again the way how you solved the puzzle?
The scientist about who you read in the magazine gave a lecture yesterday. 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: ②는 'Jake is more careful than his brother is'라는 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 쓰여 어법상 맞다. ①은 'lives across the street'가 주어 'The man'을 꾸며주는 관계사절인데 관계대명사 who가 빠져 있어 틀리다(The man who lives across the street). ③은 선행사 'restaurant'가 있으므로 관계대명사 what을 쓸 수 없고 that을 써야 한다. ④는 'the way'와 관계부사 'how'를 함께 쓸 수 없으므로 둘 중 하나만 남겨야 한다(the way that / how). ⑤는 전치사 about 뒤에는 목적격 관계대명사 whom을 써야 하므로 who를 whom으로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Transporting millions of commuters every day takes a serious toll on our cities. Our current transportation methods cause problems with traffic jams, air pollution, and noise. But there are some creative solutions! (A)One possible solution is bike-sharing, and it promises to make our commutes as convenient as possible. Bike-sharing stations are placed throughout downtown areas, ⓐwhich shortens the time people spend waiting for transportation. This allows commuters to travel quickly to their destinations. Another benefit is that it reduces the number of cars on the road, ⓑwhich creates quieter streets for pedestrians.

밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ가 각각 가리키는 것을 찾아 우리말로 쓰시오.
ⓐ _____
ⓑ _____
answer: ⓐ 자전거 공유 정류장이 시내 곳곳에 설치된다는 것, ⓑ (자 전거 공유가) 도로 위의 차량 수를 줄인다는 것
solution: ⓐ와 ⓑ의 which는 특정 명사가 아니라 앞에 나온 절 전체의 내용을 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Transporting millions of commuters every day takes a serious toll on our cities. Our current transportation methods cause problems with traffic jams, air pollution, and noise. But there are some creative solutions! (A)One possible solution is bike-sharing, and it promises to make our commutes as convenient as possible. Bike-sharing stations are placed throughout downtown areas, ⓐwhich shortens the time people spend waiting for transportation. This allows commuters to travel quickly to their destinations. Another benefit is that it reduces the number of cars on the road, ⓑwhich creates quieter streets for pedestrians.

밑줄 친 문장 (A)을 관계사를 이용하여 다시 쓰시오.
→ _____
answer: Bike-sharing, which promises to make our commutes as convenient as possible, is one possible solution.
solution: 두 개의 절을 접속사 and로 연결한 문장을 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 사용해 한 문장으로 결합한다. it은 앞의 명사 bike-sharing을 가리키므로 콤마 뒤에 which를 써서 삽입절을 만든다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분을 어법상 잘못 고친 것은?
A protein in the venom of cone snails could help chronic pain patients ⓐmanaged their symptoms without addictive drugs. Chronic pain occurs when nerve cells continue sending pain signals to the brain long after an injury has healed. The protein in snail venom makes these nerve cells
ⓑstopping the signals immediately, so patients can continue ⓒfunction normally in daily life. Researchers think the same protein may be able to relieve pain in humans without causing dependence. Fortunately the protein would
ⓓturned into a simple pill, and patients would not be required ⓔreceiving painful injections. * venom 독 / chronic 만성의
solution: ③ continue는 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 'function'은 'to function' 또는 'functioning'으로 고쳐야 한다. 그런데 이를 과거형 'functioned'로 잘못 고쳤으므로 어법상 틀린 수정이다. ① 'help + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조이므로 'managed'는 'manage'로 고치는 것이 옳다. ② 'make + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조이므로 'stopping'은 'stop'으로 고치는 것이 옳다. ④ 조동사 would 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 수동태 'be turned'로 고치는 것이 옳다. ⑤ 'be required + to부정사' 구조이므로 'receiving'은 'to receive'로 고치는 것이 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:

• Don't _____ her cry again.

choices: make(s) 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: ⑤ 첫 번째 문장은 make + 목적어 + 형용사, 두 번째 문장은 make + 목적어 + 동사원형, 세 번째 문장은 ‘만들다’의 의미로 쓰이므로 세 문장에 모두 들어갈 수 있는 말은 make(s)이다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법상 바른 것끼리 묶인 것은?
보기 ⓐThe teacher let the students to leave early.
ⓑThe tutor helped him to solve the difficult problem.
ⓒWe heard the choir singing beautifully.
ⓓThe counselor advised her join the debate club.
ⓔThe feedback kept the students focused during the exam.
solution: ⓑ help + 목적어 + (to)부정사 구조로 to solve가 알맞다. ⓒ 지각동사 hear는 목적어 + 현재분사를 취할 수 있으므로 singing이 알맞다. ⓔ keep + 목적어 + 과거분사/형용사에서 focused가 학생들의 상태를 나타내므로 알맞다. ⓐ to leave → leave 사역동사 let은 목적격보어로 원형부정사를 취한다. ⓓ join → to join advise + 목적어 + to부정사 구조를 써야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 맞는 것을 두 개 고르면?
Remember that patience is essential when resolving a conflict between siblings. If your apology is not accepted right away, thank your brother for listening to you and ⓐleft the door open for future reconciliation. Keep in mind ⓑthat just because a sibling accepts your apology does not mean he has fully forgiven you. It can take time, maybe a long time, before the ⓒhurting sibling can completely trust you again. There is
ⓓlittle you can do to speed up this process. If the relationship truly matters to you, it is worth giving him the time and space needed to heal. Do not expect him ⓔgo back to normal immediately.
① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
solution: 정답은 ②, ④이다. ②는 the fact에 해당하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 올바르게 쓰였다. ④는 you can do가 불가산적 개념이므로 little이 올바르게 쓰였다. ①은 'thank ~ for listening ... and leaving ...'처럼 동명사로 병렬되어야 하는데 과거형 left가 쓰여 병렬 구조가 깨져 어법상 틀리다. ③은 '상처받은 형제'라는 의미이므로 과거분사 hurt가 되어야 하는데 현재분사 hurting이 쓰여 어법상 틀리다. ⑤는 'expect + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조가 되어야 하므로 go 앞에 to가 필요한데 빠져 있어 어법상 틀리다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중, 어법상 옳은 문장을 모두 고르면?
① Since the new intern kept mixing up the files, he was eventually made to reorganize the entire cabinet by himself.
② After hearing the surprising news, the whole team looked confusing during the meeting.
③ Given how quiet the office was this morning, the manager must have left early for a client visit.
④ Have you ever heard your coworkers in a crowded office to complain about the noise?
⑤ Instead of complaining about the heavy workload, she stayed calm despite not being able to finish everything by noon.
solution: ① 사동사 make의 수동태 be made to+동사원형 (reorganize) 구조가 올바르게 쓰였으므로 옳다. ③ 과거 사실에 대한 강한 추측을 나타내는 must have+p.p. (left) 구조가 올바르게 쓰였으므로 옳다. ⑤ 전치사 instead of, despite 뒤에 각각 동명사 complaining, not being able to+동사원형 구조가 올바르게 쓰였으므로 옳다. ② 감정을 느끼는 주체 team을 수식하므로 confused(감정을 느끼는)가 되어야 하며, confusing(감정을 일으키는)은 틀렸다. ④ heard(지각동사) 뒤 목적격 보어로 to complain이 아니라 원형부정사나 현재분사인 complain 또는 complaining이 와야 하므로 틀렸다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 2개 고르면?
Money was once viewed merely as a tool for barter in ancient marketplaces. As barter systems
ⓐdeclined in early civilizations, currency began to be used for trade. Merchants and traders believed ⓑthat coins were more reliable than goods, especially when trading across long distances. The powerful did all they could to control minting, perhaps except for a small transaction, ⓒit was regarded as harmless. Later, as paper money and banknotes ⓓreplacing metal coins across kingdoms, currency in modern society was viewed as a symbol of trust. Their innovations influenced economists such as Adam Smith, whose theories ⓔwere praised for explaining the value of money.
① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복

We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times ⓐbiggest than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile ⓑby compare the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth
ⓒbe carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. 실전 학습 The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people ⓓto relaxing in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration.
Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began ⓔused smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ 'demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled'에서 동사 demand는 당위적 의미를 나타내어 that절에 '(should +) 동사원형'을 요구하는 당위적 가정법을 취한다. 따라서 be가 원형동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ① biggest → bigger 배수 표현(ten times)과 함께 두 대상을 비교할 때는 반드시 비교급을 사용해야 한다. 최상급 biggest는 세 개 이상을 비교할 때 쓰이므로 비교급 bigger로 고쳐야 한다. ② by compare → by comparing 전치사 by 뒤에는 동사원형이 아닌 동명사(v-ing)가 와야 한다. 따라서 compare를 comparing으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ to relaxing → to relax get + 목적어 + to부정사 구조에서 목적격보어로는 'to + 동사원형'이 와야 한다. to 뒤에 동명사 relaxing을 쓸 수 없으므로 to relax로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ used → using began 뒤에는 동명사(v-ing) 또는 to부정사가 목적어로 올 수 있지만, 과거분사 used는 목적어 자리에 올 수 없다. 따라서 using으로 고쳐야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and
ⓐunique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out ⓑwhat they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. Vincent van Gogh The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 ⓒof which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy ⓓconveying. Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings ⓔdepicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with own. 3과. The Gift of Art _____ 실전 학습 _____ , _____ → _____ , _____ →
solution: ⓑ what → how "find out" 뒤에 이어지는 절 "they were a source of inspiration"은 주어(they)와 동사(were), 보어(a source of inspiration)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장 구조이다. 따라서 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 '어떻게 ~였는지'의 의미를 나타내는 how가 적절하다. what은 명사절 안에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데, 뒤 절이 이미 완전하므로 what은 올 수 없다. ⓓ conveying → being conveyed "his joy"는 색깔들의 조합에 의해 '전달되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 따라서 능동형 현재분사 conveying이 아니라 수동의 의미를 가진 being conveyed가 올바르다. ⓐ "unique"는 앞의 형용사 "interesting"과 병렬 구조를 이루며 명사 "colors"를 수식하는 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ "of which"는 선행사 "900 paintings" 중 일부인 "300"을 나타내는 [수사 + of which] 구조의 관계대명사구로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ "depicting"은 앞의 명사 "paintings"를 수식하는 현재분사로, paintings가 능동적으로 도시 장면을 묘사하는 주체이므로 올바르게 쓰였다.

Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, ⓐknowing as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night,
ⓑsuggested the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows ⓒhow the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest
ⓓturned bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork
ⓔto come to you. You may love it or you may hate it, but art will always take you to a place beyond everyday life.

solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments.에서 'shows'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 how가 쓰였다. 'how + 주어 + 동사'의 간접의문문 구조로, 동사 shows의 목적어절을 올바르게 이끌고 있어 어법상 옳다. 학생들이 what이나 that으로 혼동하기 쉽지만, '어떻게 화가가 아름다운 가을의 순간들을 기렸는지'라는 방법의 의미로 how가 적절하다. ① knowing as → known as R.C. Gorman은 '피카소로 알려진' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 주어(R.C. Gorman)와 분사의 관계가 수동(~ 로 알려진)이므로 현재분사 knowing이 아닌 과거분사 known을 써야 한다. 'be known as'의 수동 관계에서 비롯된 과거분사구문이어야 하므로 knowing as를 known as로 고쳐야 한다. ② suggested → suggesting 문장의 주어인 'Her figure in a red dress'가 능동적으로 '암시하는' 행위를 하는 것이므로 능동의 분사구문이 필요하다. 과거분사 suggested는 수동의 의미(~되어진)를 나타내므로 문맥과 맞지 않는다. 능동의 현재분사 suggesting으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ turned → turns 이 문장은 그림이 묘사하는 내용을 현재시제로 서술하는 문맥이다. 같은 절 내 'is reflected'가 현재시제로 쓰여 있고, 앞 문장들도 현재시제로 일관되게 서술하고 있으므로, when절의 동사도 현재시제 turns로 써야 한다. 과거시제 turned는 이 문맥에서 어법상 적절하지 않다. ⑤ to come → come 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)을 취한다. 'let + 목적어 + 동사원형'의 구조이므로, to come이 아닌 원형부정사 come을 써야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings ⓐdepicted urban scenes that ⓑshowing how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, ⓒemphasized how people can be in the same space and feel
ⓓapart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors
ⓔcontrasts with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
solution: ④ 'feel apart'에서 apart는 '서로 떨어져 있는'이라는 의미의 서술적 표현으로, feel의 보어 자리에 올바르게 쓰였다. 따라서 ④가 정답이다. ① depicted → depicting 'paintings'를 수식하는 분사 자리로, paintings가 직접 도시 장면을 '묘사하는' 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사 depicting이 와야 한다. 과거분사 depicted는 수동의 의미(묘사되어진)를 나타내므로 어법상 틀렸다. ② showing → showed 'urban scenes that '에서 that은 주격 관계대명사이고, 관계절 안에서 동사 역할을 해야 한다. showing은 동사 기능을 할 수 없으므로 어법상 틀렸다. 시제에 맞는 동사 showed로 고쳐야 한다. ③ emphasized → emphasizing 앞 절(The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside)의 내용을 부연하는 분사구문 자리이다. 의미상 주어인 'The bright yellow walls'가 능동적으로 강조하는 주체이므로 현재분사 emphasizing이 와야 한다. 과거분사 emphasized는 수동의 의미여서 어법상 틀렸다. ⑤ contrasts → contrast 주어인 'the cool shades of the other colors'의 핵심 명사는 복수명사 shades이므로 동사도 복수형 contrast가 와야 한다. 단수 동사 contrasts는 수일치 오류이다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings ⓐdepicting urban scenes ⓑwho showed ⓒhow even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, ⓓemphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights ⓔlead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
solution: ② who showed → that showed (또는 which showed) 선행사인 'urban scenes'는 사물이므로 사람을 받는 주격 관계대명사 who를 쓸 수 없다. 사물 선행사에는 관계대명사 that 또는 which를 써야 한다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① 'he created paintings depicting urban scenes'에서 depicting은 paintings를 후치 수식하는 현재분사이다. paintings가 urban scenes를 '묘사하는' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 depicting이 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 'showed how even familiar surroundings could cause …'에서 how는 showed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 'emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart'에서 emphasizing은 앞 절 전체 내용을 부연하는 분사구문으로, 주어인 The bright yellow walls가 능동적으로 강조하는 주체이므로 현재분사 emphasizing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 'The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye'에서 주어 The yellow lights는 복수 명사이므로 동사원형 lead가 올바르게 쓰였다.
